description: Master NFR List: a structured knowledge base of non-functional requirements, not an analysis component. Layer one is a generic baseline that applies to every service. Layer two is a set of tech-stack modules that extend the baseline. Cross-cutting modules apply to every service and are evaluated against the Stage 1 dataset (each entry lists the dataset paths and the pass criteria). Stage 3 loads this file and evaluates the applicable modules; this file itself judges nothing.

layers.baseline: Generic requirements that hold regardless of tech stack.
layers.tech_stack: Modules that extend the baseline for one technology. Applied only when the Stage 1 fingerprint detects it.
layers.cross_cutting: Modules that apply to every service and are evaluated against Stage 1 infrastructure, pipeline, dependency, secrets and encryption data.

baseline.title: Generic baseline
baseline.description: Non-functional requirements that apply regardless of tech stack. Tech-stack modules extend these entries.

entry_extensions.applies_to_layer: which layer the requirement is enforced at: application | platform | both | process

entries.title: Bounded retries with backoff for transient failures
entries.requirement: Calls to remote dependencies that can fail transiently retry a bounded number of times (a small fixed attempt count) using exponential backoff with jitter, and only on errors that are actually transient.
entries.best_practice: Never retry unbounded or with a fixed delay; add jitter to avoid synchronized retry storms; retry only idempotent operations or those protected by an idempotency key; enforce an overall deadline so retries cannot outlast the caller's own timeout; keep retries at one layer of the call chain to avoid multiplicative amplification.
entries.audit_requirement: Retry policy per dependency is documented and reviewed as part of design sign-off.

monitoring.signal: retry attempt counter by outcome
monitoring.detail: e.g. resilience4j.retry.calls or the client library's retry metric

monitoring.signal: failure rate and response time of the downstream service call

verification.criteria: Every outbound dependency in the transaction flows is covered by a retry pattern in code or a mesh retry policy, with a bounded attempt count; non-idempotent calls are not retried blindly.

entries.title: Idempotency of retried and redelivered operations
entries.requirement: Any operation that can be retried by the client, a gateway, the mesh or a message broker is idempotent or deduplicates through an idempotency key.
entries.best_practice: Use natural idempotency (PUT semantics, upserts) or an idempotency-key store with a TTL; make consumers tolerate duplicate delivery.
entries.audit_requirement: Financial and other regulated writes record the idempotency key with the transaction for reconciliation.

monitoring.signal: duplicate request or duplicate message detected counter
idempotency-key reuse events

verification.criteria: Write entry points that are retried or consumed from a broker show an idempotency mechanism or are inherently idempotent.

entries.title: Circuit breaker on remote dependencies
entries.requirement: Each remote dependency whose failure or slowness would otherwise consume caller resources is wrapped in a circuit breaker (in code or at the mesh layer) that fails fast when the dependency is unhealthy.
entries.best_practice: Combine the breaker with a timeout, a bulkhead and a defined fallback or degraded response; tune failure-rate and slow-call thresholds per dependency; use half-open probing; expose breaker state as a metric.
entries.audit_requirement: Breaker thresholds and fallback behaviour are recorded per dependency in the service's resilience design.

monitoring.signal: circuit breaker state and failure rate
response time and failure rate of the dependency's service

verification.criteria: Each dependency classified as hard_failure or gracefully_degradable has a circuit breaker in code or a mesh circuit_breaker policy, or a recorded reason why not.

entries.title: Explicit timeouts on every outbound call
entries.requirement: Every network call (HTTP, gRPC, database, cache, messaging) has an explicit connect timeout and an explicit read or request timeout; none relies on an infinite or library default.
entries.best_practice: Set timeouts from the dependency's observed latency percentiles plus headroom; keep them shorter than the caller's own timeout; configure them centrally per client rather than per call site.
entries.audit_requirement: Timeout values are reviewed with the dependency owner and recorded per dependency.

monitoring.signal: service response time percentiles and failure rate per downstream call
client timeout counters

verification.criteria: Each outbound dependency in the flow map has a timeout pattern in code or configuration, or a mesh timeout policy.

entries.title: Timeout budget that shrinks down the call chain
entries.requirement: Timeouts nest: a caller's timeout is larger than the sum of its downstream timeouts and retries, and deadlines are propagated rather than restarted at each hop.
entries.best_practice: Propagate a request deadline (for example gRPC deadlines or a header) and derive downstream timeouts from the remaining budget; avoid client, gateway and mesh timeouts that disagree.

monitoring.signal: distributed traces showing where in the chain time is spent
requests that exceeded their deadline

verification.criteria: Timeout values at gateway, mesh and client layers are consistent (outer larger than inner).

entries.title: Separate liveness and readiness health endpoints
entries.requirement: The service exposes a liveness signal (the process is alive) and a readiness signal (it can take traffic), consumed by the platform's probes.
entries.best_practice: Liveness must not depend on downstream services (a dependency outage must not restart healthy pods); readiness reflects ability to serve; add a startup probe for slow starts; keep health endpoints cheap and unauthenticated on an internal port.

monitoring.signal: probe failures and restart counts
monitoring.detail: container restart counts or Dynatrace Kubernetes events

monitoring.signal: process availability

verification.criteria: Every workload container defines liveness and readiness probes, and the application exposes matching endpoints.

entries.title: Readiness reflects dependency health without cascading
entries.requirement: Readiness may include critical dependencies but must degrade traffic gracefully, not flap all replicas at once when a shared dependency blips.
entries.best_practice: Check only dependencies without which the service cannot serve; add hysteresis (failure thresholds); prefer circuit breakers to health-check coupling for optional dependencies.

monitoring.signal: number of ready replicas over time
readiness state transitions with reason

verification.criteria: Readiness probe configuration uses failure thresholds and does not include dependencies classified as gracefully_degradable.

entries.title: Structured logging with a standard schema
entries.requirement: Logs are structured (JSON or key-value), carry timestamp, level, service name, version, environment and message, and go to stdout or a collector, not local files that vanish with the container.
entries.best_practice: Use one logging library and format across services; log at INFO by default with per-package override; avoid multi-line stack traces that break parsing.
entries.audit_requirement: Log retention meets the organisation's policy and is set explicitly in the log platform.

monitoring.signal: log volume by level and service
log event counters by level

verification.criteria: A structured logging configuration or encoder is present in the application; retention is configured where logs are collected.

entries.title: Trace and correlation identifiers in every log line
entries.requirement: Each log line carries the trace id (and span id) or a request correlation id that is propagated across service calls.
entries.best_practice: Use W3C Trace Context; inject the ids into the logging MDC/context automatically; return the id to callers in error responses.
entries.audit_requirement: Correlation ids allow an audited transaction to be reconstructed across services.

monitoring.signal: log-to-trace correlation for supported logging frameworks
share of log lines carrying a trace id

verification.criteria: Sampled log output contains a trace or correlation id that matches the distributed trace.

entries.title: No secrets or personal data in logs
entries.requirement: Credentials, tokens, full card numbers and unmasked personal data are never written to logs.
entries.best_practice: Mask at the logging layer with allow-lists for fields; never log full request or response bodies by default; scan logs in CI or with the log platform's sensitive-data rules.
entries.audit_requirement: Periodic log review evidences absence of sensitive data (privacy and PCI-style controls).

monitoring.signal: sensitive-data detector matches in log stream

verification.criteria: Logging configuration masks sensitive fields and no log statement prints secrets or full payloads.

entries.title: RED metrics for every service entry point
entries.requirement: Request rate, error rate and duration are measured and visible for each externally reachable entry point.
entries.best_practice: Use histograms/percentiles rather than averages; break down by route and status class; alert on symptoms (error ratio, latency SLO burn) not causes.

monitoring.signal: service request count, response time and failure rate
http server request timer

verification.criteria: An observability provider is bound to the service and its entry points have request metrics available (default or library emitted).

entries.title: Saturation metrics for constrained resources
entries.requirement: Utilisation of CPU, memory, connection pools, thread pools and queues is measured against their limits.
entries.best_practice: Alert before saturation (for example pool wait time, queue depth) rather than at failure; compare against configured limits, not host capacity.

monitoring.signal: process CPU, memory, JVM/runtime memory and GC
connection pool and thread pool gauges

verification.criteria: Each configured pool, executor and resource limit has a corresponding utilisation metric available.

entries.title: SLOs and symptom-based alerting
entries.requirement: Each user-facing capability has at least one SLO (availability and latency) with burn-rate alerting and a named owner.
entries.best_practice: Derive SLOs from business context; use multi-window burn-rate alerts; link each alert to a runbook.
entries.audit_requirement: SLO definitions and review history are retained.

monitoring.signal: SLO status and burn rate in the observability platform

verification.criteria: An SLO exists for each key business operation identified in the business context.

entries.title: Dependency call visibility
entries.requirement: Every dependency in the transaction flow map has request rate, latency and error visibility from the calling service.
entries.best_practice: Rely on automatic instrumentation for standard clients; add custom spans or metrics only for clients that are not auto-instrumented.

monitoring.signal: outbound call metrics and service topology
metrics for clients that OneAgent does not instrument

verification.criteria: Each dependency named in the flow map is visible in the provider's topology with metrics.

entries.title: Graceful shutdown and connection draining
entries.requirement: On termination the service stops accepting new work, finishes or hands off in-flight work within a bounded time, and closes connections cleanly.
entries.best_practice: Handle SIGTERM; set the platform grace period above the drain time; deregister from load balancing first (preStop delay); commit or abort in-flight messages deterministically.

monitoring.signal: requests failed during rollout
monitoring.detail: error-rate spikes correlated with deployment events

verification.criteria: A termination grace period is set explicitly and the application enables graceful shutdown.

lang_java.title: Java
lang_java.description: JVM runtime requirements for services written in Java (and other JVM languages built with Maven or Gradle).

entry_extensions.jvm_flag: the JVM option or system property the requirement is expressed through, where there is one

entries.title: Container-aware heap sizing
entries.requirement: The JVM heap is sized relative to the container memory limit (for example a percentage of container memory), with explicit headroom for metaspace, thread stacks, direct buffers and code cache.
entries.best_practice: Use -XX:MaxRAMPercentage (commonly 60 to 75 percent) or explicit -Xmx below the limit; set -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError so the platform restarts a failed JVM; do not let heap plus non-heap exceed the container limit.

monitoring.signal: JVM memory pool usage and container memory working set
jvm.memory.used and jvm.memory.max

verification.criteria: Container memory limits are set, and the start command or JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS sets heap relative to them.

entries.title: Supported long-term-support Java version
entries.requirement: The service targets a Java version that still receives security updates (a current LTS release).
entries.best_practice: Track the LTS cadence; keep base images patched; avoid running end-of-life major versions in production.
entries.audit_requirement: Runtime versions are inventoried for vulnerability management.

monitoring.signal: JVM version reported per process

verification.criteria: runtime_versions.java is a currently supported LTS release.

entries.title: Garbage collector chosen and GC health monitored
entries.requirement: The garbage collector is chosen deliberately for the workload (latency versus throughput) and GC pause time and frequency are monitored against a budget.
entries.best_practice: G1 as a general default; consider ZGC or Shenandoah for strict latency; enable GC logging; alert on sustained pause time and allocation-rate growth.

monitoring.signal: GC collection time, count and suspension time
jvm.gc.pause and jvm.gc.memory.allocated

verification.criteria: GC pause percentiles stay within the latency budget under load.

entries.title: Bounded executors and no unbounded thread creation
entries.requirement: Application code uses bounded thread pools with bounded queues and a rejection policy, and blocking work does not run on request or event-loop threads.
entries.best_practice: Avoid Executors.newCachedThreadPool and unbounded queues; name pools; for virtual threads, still bound concurrency towards downstream systems.

monitoring.signal: JVM thread count
executor active, queued and completed counts

verification.criteria: thread_pool capacity settings are explicit and bounded.

entries.title: Dependency vulnerability scanning in the build
entries.requirement: Third-party dependencies are scanned for known vulnerabilities on every build, with a defined remediation time by severity, and dependency versions are managed through a BOM or dependency management section.
entries.best_practice: Use software composition analysis in CI; generate an SBOM; update through automated pull requests.
entries.audit_requirement: Scan results and exceptions are retained per release.

monitoring.signal: open vulnerabilities by severity and age

verification.criteria: A dependency scan step exists in the pipeline; dependency versions are resolved.

lang_python.title: Python
lang_python.description: Runtime requirements for Python services (web frameworks such as Django, Flask and FastAPI are covered here).

entries.title: Supported Python version
entries.requirement: The service runs on a Python version that still receives security fixes.
entries.best_practice: Track upstream support windows; test on the target version in CI; keep the base image patched.
entries.audit_requirement: Runtime versions are inventoried for vulnerability management.

monitoring.signal: Python version reported per process

verification.criteria: The declared Python version is within upstream security support.

entries.title: Production application server with explicit worker configuration
entries.requirement: The service runs under a production WSGI or ASGI server (for example gunicorn or uvicorn) with explicit worker count, worker class, timeout and graceful timeout, never the framework's development server.
entries.best_practice: Size workers to the container CPU limit; set request timeouts; recycle workers (max requests with jitter) to bound memory growth; preload carefully.

monitoring.signal: process CPU and memory per worker process
worker busy and queue metrics
monitoring.detail: from the server's own statsd or Prometheus support

verification.criteria: An application server package is a dependency and the container entrypoint starts it with explicit worker settings.

entries.title: Explicit timeouts on HTTP and database clients
entries.requirement: Every outbound call passes a timeout; the requests library has no default timeout, and database drivers and pools have explicit connect and statement timeouts.
entries.best_practice: Wrap clients in a shared session with a default timeout tuple (connect, read); use retries via urllib3 Retry or tenacity with bounded attempts.

monitoring.signal: outbound request response time and failure rate

verification.criteria: Each outbound HTTP or database call in the flows has a timeout pattern.

entries.title: Blocking calls kept out of the event loop
entries.requirement: In async services, blocking I/O or CPU-heavy work runs in a thread or process pool rather than on the event loop.
entries.best_practice: Use async drivers or run_in_executor; monitor event loop lag; keep synchronous and asynchronous endpoints separate.

monitoring.signal: event loop lag
service response time percentiles

verification.criteria: Async handlers contain no blocking calls (review of the flow map's steps).

entries.title: Reproducible, pinned dependencies
entries.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in a lock file (ideally with hashes) and installed from it in the build.
entries.best_practice: Use a lock file tool (pip-tools, Poetry, uv); scan the lock file for vulnerabilities; build wheels in a multi-stage image.
entries.audit_requirement: SBOM retained per release.

monitoring.signal: vulnerable dependency count

verification.criteria: A lock or pinned requirements file exists and dependency versions are exact.

lang_javascript_typescript.title: JavaScript / TypeScript (Node.js)
lang_javascript_typescript.description: Runtime requirements for Node.js services written in JavaScript or TypeScript (Express, NestJS, Next.js and similar are covered here).

entries.title: Supported Node.js LTS runtime
entries.requirement: The service runs on a Node.js release line that is in active or maintenance LTS.
entries.best_practice: Pin the version in the manifest (engines) and the base image; upgrade on the LTS cadence; run with NODE_ENV=production.
entries.audit_requirement: Runtime versions are inventoried for vulnerability management.

monitoring.signal: Node.js version reported per process

verification.criteria: An engines or runtime version is declared and is an LTS line.

entries.title: Process-level error handling and graceful shutdown
entries.requirement: Unhandled promise rejections and uncaught exceptions are handled deliberately (log, then exit so the platform restarts), and SIGTERM triggers a graceful drain of the HTTP server and connections.
entries.best_practice: Register handlers for unhandledRejection, uncaughtException and SIGTERM; close the server and pools before exit; run node directly as PID 1 or use an init.

monitoring.signal: process restarts and availability
unhandled rejection and uncaught exception events

verification.criteria: Shutdown handlers exist and the grace period is set.

entries.title: Event loop kept responsive
entries.requirement: CPU-heavy or synchronous work does not block the event loop; event loop lag is monitored against a budget.
entries.best_practice: Offload heavy work to worker threads or separate services; avoid synchronous fs and crypto calls on request paths; monitor event loop delay.

monitoring.signal: Node.js event loop and V8 heap metrics
nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds

verification.criteria: Event loop lag percentiles stay within budget under load.

entries.title: Timeouts and connection reuse on outbound HTTP clients
entries.requirement: Outbound HTTP calls set a timeout (axios and fetch have none by default) and reuse connections through a keep-alive agent with bounded sockets.
entries.best_practice: Use AbortSignal.timeout or client timeout options; configure a shared agent (maxSockets); add bounded retries with jitter.

monitoring.signal: outbound request response time and failure rate

verification.criteria: Each outbound HTTP call in the flows has a timeout pattern.

entries.title: Memory limit aligned with V8 heap
entries.requirement: The V8 old-space limit is set relative to the container memory limit so the process is not OOM-killed unpredictably.
entries.best_practice: Set --max-old-space-size to roughly 75 percent of the container limit; monitor heap used against it.

monitoring.signal: V8 heap memory and process working set

verification.criteria: Container memory limit and Node heap flag are both set and consistent.

entries.title: Locked and audited dependencies, strict typing
entries.requirement: A lock file is committed and used for installs (npm ci), dependencies are audited on every build, and TypeScript projects compile with strict mode.
entries.best_practice: Use npm ci or the equivalent frozen install; automated dependency updates; block builds on high-severity advisories.
entries.audit_requirement: SBOM and audit results retained per release.

monitoring.signal: vulnerable dependency count

verification.criteria: A lock file exists and dependency versions are pinned.

lang_go.title: Go
lang_go.description: Runtime requirements for services written in Go (net/http, Gin, Echo, Fiber, Chi and similar are covered here).

entries.title: Context deadlines and explicit server and client timeouts
entries.requirement: Every outbound call carries a context with a deadline, http.Client has a Timeout, and http.Server sets ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout and IdleTimeout (the defaults are none).
entries.best_practice: Derive downstream deadlines from the request context; cancel on client disconnect; never use http.DefaultClient in production code.

monitoring.signal: request response time and failure rate
monitoring.detail: for standard library HTTP servers and clients

verification.criteria: Server and client timeouts are configured in code.

entries.title: Bounded concurrency and no goroutine leaks
entries.requirement: Goroutine creation on request paths is bounded (worker pools, semaphores, errgroup limits), every goroutine has a termination condition, and goroutine count is monitored.
entries.best_practice: Pass context to every goroutine; use errgroup with SetLimit; test with goleak; alert on monotonic goroutine growth.

monitoring.signal: go_goroutines
goroutine count where the Go sensor is active

verification.criteria: Goroutine count is stable under steady load and no unbounded spawn per request is present.

entries.title: Container-aware GOMAXPROCS and memory limit
entries.requirement: GOMAXPROCS matches the container CPU limit and GOMEMLIMIT is set below the container memory limit, so the scheduler and garbage collector respect the container.
entries.best_practice: Use a Go release with container-aware GOMAXPROCS or automaxprocs; set GOMEMLIMIT to roughly 90 percent of the limit; monitor GC CPU share.

monitoring.signal: go_memstats and go_gc_duration_seconds

verification.criteria: CPU and memory limits are set and the runtime honours them.

entries.title: Graceful shutdown of servers and workers
entries.requirement: On SIGTERM the service calls Server.Shutdown with a timeout, stops consumers and background workers, and flushes telemetry before exit.
entries.best_practice: Use signal.NotifyContext; align the shutdown timeout with terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

monitoring.signal: errors during rollouts

verification.criteria: Shutdown handling exists and the grace period exceeds the shutdown timeout.

entries.title: Diagnostics endpoints protected
entries.requirement: pprof and expvar endpoints are not exposed on the public listener; where enabled they bind to a separate internal port.
entries.best_practice: Serve diagnostics on localhost or an authenticated admin port; enable continuous profiling through the platform instead.
entries.audit_requirement: Access to diagnostics endpoints is logged.

monitoring.signal: requests to /debug endpoints

verification.criteria: Diagnostics endpoints are not reachable from the public listener.

lang_rust.title: Rust
lang_rust.description: Runtime requirements for services written in Rust (Axum, Actix Web, Rocket, Tonic and Tokio-based services are covered here).

entries.title: No panics on request paths; errors are typed and handled
entries.requirement: Request handling returns errors as values mapped to responses; panics are contained (catch-panic layer or task boundary) and never take down the process.
entries.best_practice: Avoid unwrap and expect on fallible input paths; use thiserror or anyhow at boundaries; set a panic hook that logs with context; decide panic=abort versus unwind deliberately.

monitoring.signal: panic events with backtrace
request error counters by error type

verification.criteria: Handlers convert errors to responses and a panic boundary exists.

entries.title: Async runtime configured and blocking work isolated
entries.requirement: The Tokio runtime has an explicit worker thread count and a bounded blocking pool, and blocking or CPU-heavy work runs in spawn_blocking or a dedicated pool.
entries.best_practice: Size workers to the container CPU limit; never block inside async tasks; monitor task and runtime metrics.

monitoring.signal: tokio runtime metrics

verification.criteria: Runtime configuration is explicit and consistent with the container CPU limit.

entries.title: Explicit timeouts on network clients
entries.requirement: HTTP, database and gRPC clients set connect and request timeouts (reqwest has no overall timeout by default) and requests are wrapped with tower or tokio timeouts.
entries.best_practice: Configure a shared client with timeouts; use tower layers for timeout, retry and concurrency limits.

monitoring.signal: client request duration and timeout counts

verification.criteria: Each outbound call in the flows has a timeout pattern.

entries.title: Telemetry exported through OpenTelemetry
entries.requirement: Because OneAgent has no code-level sensor for Rust, traces and metrics are produced with tracing and OpenTelemetry and exported over OTLP to the observability platform.
entries.best_practice: Use tracing spans with W3C trace context propagation; export via an OTLP endpoint (collector or platform ingest); include service name and version resource attributes.

monitoring.signal: OTLP traces and metrics from the service
host and process level metrics only

verification.criteria: An OpenTelemetry or tracing dependency and exporter configuration exist.

entries.title: Dependency and license audit, release profile
entries.requirement: Dependencies are audited (RustSec advisories, licenses) on every build, Cargo.lock is committed for binaries, and production builds use the release profile with overflow checks decided deliberately.
entries.best_practice: Run cargo audit and cargo deny in CI; pin toolchain via rust-toolchain; produce a minimal static or distroless image.
entries.audit_requirement: Audit output retained per release.

monitoring.signal: advisory count by severity

verification.criteria: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are present with resolved versions.

spring_boot.title: Spring Boot
spring_boot.description: Requirements specific to Spring Boot services (Spring MVC, WebFlux, Spring Data, Actuator, Spring Cache). Extends the baseline.

entry_extensions.spring_property: the Spring property or annotation the requirement is expressed through

entries.title: Actuator health groups for liveness and readiness
entries.requirement: Spring Boot Actuator is present with liveness and readiness health groups enabled, and the Kubernetes probes call them (/actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness).
entries.best_practice: Keep the liveness group free of external dependencies; include only critical dependencies in readiness; expose health on the management port; show details only to authorised callers.

monitoring.signal: probe results and pod restarts
health status gauge

verification.criteria: spring-boot-starter-actuator is a dependency and each container has liveness and readiness probes pointing at actuator health endpoints (health_probes_and_application_health cross reference).

entries.title: Actuator endpoints exposed minimally and protected
entries.requirement: Only the actuator endpoints that are needed (health, info, metrics or prometheus) are exposed over HTTP, on a management port or path that is not publicly routable, and sensitive endpoints (env, heapdump, threaddump, loggers, shutdown) are not exposed or are authenticated.
entries.best_practice: Use a separate management port with network policy; secure with Spring Security; disable info leaks such as full health details.
entries.audit_requirement: Access to management endpoints is logged.

monitoring.signal: requests to actuator endpoints by caller

verification.criteria: Exposure configuration lists a minimal set and the ingress does not route to the management path.

entries.title: Graceful shutdown enabled
entries.requirement: server.shutdown is graceful with a shutdown phase timeout shorter than the Kubernetes termination grace period.
entries.best_practice: Combine with a preStop sleep so the endpoint is removed from load balancing before the server stops accepting requests.

monitoring.signal: failure rate during rollout windows

verification.criteria: server.shutdown=graceful is set (default is immediate in older versions) and the grace period exceeds the phase timeout.

entries.title: Connection pool and server thread settings explicit
entries.requirement: HikariCP maximum pool size, connection timeout and max lifetime, and the embedded server's thread and connection limits, are set explicitly.
entries.best_practice: Pool size from the database connection budget; Tomcat threads consistent with CPU; keep max-lifetime below database and proxy idle timeouts.

monitoring.signal: hikaricp.connections.active, pending and timeout
tomcat.threads.busy and current

verification.criteria: db_pool and server_connections settings have origin explicit.

entries.title: Timeouts on RestClient, RestTemplate and WebClient
entries.requirement: Every RestClient, RestTemplate and WebClient bean has explicit connect and read timeouts through its request factory or HTTP client (the defaults are effectively unlimited).
entries.best_practice: Configure through a shared builder or the Spring Boot HTTP client settings; add resilience with Resilience4j or Spring Retry; propagate trace context.

monitoring.signal: http.client.requests timer by outcome
outbound call response time and failure rate

verification.criteria: Each http_service dependency in the flows has a timeout pattern.

entries.title: Spring Cache bounded and expiring
entries.requirement: Caches used through the Spring Cache abstraction have a maximum size and an expiry (TTL) configured, and cache failure does not fail the request when the source of truth is available.
entries.best_practice: Use a bounded provider such as Caffeine with maximumSize and expireAfterWrite; enable statistics for hit ratio; cache errors should be logged and bypassed.
entries.audit_requirement: Cached data classes are reviewed for sensitivity.

monitoring.signal: cache.gets by result, cache.size and cache.evictions
monitoring.detail: statistics must be enabled for the provider

verification.criteria: Each cache pattern found lists a size bound and TTL in parameters, or configuration for the cache provider exists.

entries.title: JPA behaviour configured for production
entries.requirement: Open-in-view is disabled so database connections are not held during view rendering, schema auto-generation (ddl-auto create, update) is off outside local development, and transactions are scoped to the service layer.
entries.best_practice: Set spring.jpa.open-in-view=false; manage schema with a migration tool; use read-only transactions for queries; watch for N+1 selects.

monitoring.signal: hikaricp.connections.usage
monitoring.detail: long usage suggests connections held across slow work

monitoring.signal: database statement count and response time per request

verification.criteria: Configuration files set open-in-view false and do not use ddl-auto create or update for production profiles.

entries.title: Micrometer registry and metric tags configured
entries.requirement: Micrometer is configured with a registry for the observability platform (or OTLP), common tags (application, environment, version), and http.server.requests histograms for the SLO percentiles that matter.
entries.best_practice: Set management.metrics.tags.*; publish percentiles or histograms selectively; keep tag cardinality bounded.

monitoring.signal: http.server.requests, jvm.*, hikaricp.*, cache.*

verification.criteria: Micrometer is present and management.metrics configuration (registry, tags, distribution) exists.

entries.title: Structured logging and production log levels
entries.requirement: Logging uses a structured format (built-in structured logging or a JSON encoder), a production root level of INFO, and no DEBUG for security or web packages.
entries.best_practice: Use the built-in ecs, gelf or logstash formats or a JSON encoder; include trace and span ids through the tracing bridge.

monitoring.signal: logback.events by level
error and warn volume

verification.criteria: Logging configuration defines a structured encoder and production-safe levels.

microservices_architecture.title: Microservices architecture
microservices_architecture.description: Requirements that arise from running many independently deployed services that call each other. Applies when the fingerprint shows inter-service communication.

entries.title: Bounded synchronous call chains and no distributed monolith
entries.requirement: Synchronous request chains across services are shallow, fan-out is bounded, and no service calls back into its own callers; long chains use asynchronous messaging or aggregation.
entries.best_practice: Prefer at most two or three hops for user requests; use parallel calls with a shared deadline; keep dependency graphs acyclic.
entries.audit_requirement: Service dependency map is reviewed at architecture change.

monitoring.signal: service topology and PurePath call depth

verification.criteria: Outbound http_service dependencies per flow are few and no cycles appear in the provider topology.

entries.title: Distributed tracing context propagated across every hop
entries.requirement: W3C trace context (or the platform's equivalent) propagates through HTTP, messaging and asynchronous boundaries so a transaction can be followed end to end.
entries.best_practice: Rely on OneAgent for automatic propagation of supported clients; add OpenTelemetry propagation for unsupported ones; propagate through message headers.
entries.audit_requirement: Trace retention supports incident review.

monitoring.signal: PurePath distributed traces and service flow

verification.criteria: Traces from an entry point include spans for each downstream service.

entries.title: Each service owns its data
entries.requirement: A service is the only writer of its data store; other services access data through its API or events, not by sharing tables.
entries.best_practice: Separate schemas or databases per service; publish change events; avoid cross-service joins and distributed transactions (use sagas or an outbox).
entries.audit_requirement: Data ownership per service is documented.

monitoring.signal: database service call topology showing which services touch each database

verification.criteria: Each database appears connected to a single service in the topology.

entries.title: Versioned contracts and backward-compatible change
entries.requirement: Interfaces between services are versioned and evolve backward-compatibly, so services can deploy independently and roll back without lockstep releases.
entries.best_practice: Additive changes only within a version; consumer-driven contract tests in CI; deprecate with telemetry on old-version use.
entries.audit_requirement: Breaking-change approvals are recorded.

monitoring.signal: calls per API version

verification.criteria: Routes carry a version and contract tests exist in the pipeline.

entries.title: Per-service SLOs and named ownership
entries.requirement: Each service has an owner, an SLO for its entry points, and an on-call route, and dependencies' SLOs are at least as strict as what depends on them.
entries.best_practice: Compute composite availability from the dependency chain; tag services with owner and tier in the observability platform.
entries.audit_requirement: Ownership and SLO records reviewed periodically.

monitoring.signal: SLO status per service

verification.criteria: Owner and SLO exist for the service and its critical dependencies.

quarkus.title: Quarkus
quarkus.description: Requirements specific to Quarkus services (JVM and native mode, SmallRye, RESTEasy Reactive, Agroal, Hibernate ORM).

entry_extensions.quarkus_property: the application.properties key the requirement is expressed through

entries.title: SmallRye Health with liveness, readiness and startup checks
entries.requirement: The quarkus-smallrye-health extension is present and the Kubernetes probes use the live, ready and started endpoints.
entries.best_practice: Keep liveness dependency-free; add readiness checks only for critical dependencies; use the started check for slow start-up.

monitoring.signal: probe results and restarts

verification.criteria: quarkus-smallrye-health is a dependency and probes point at /q/health paths.

entries.title: Datasource pool and HTTP limits explicit
entries.requirement: Agroal pool sizes and acquisition timeout, event-loop and worker thread counts, and HTTP limits are set explicitly.
entries.best_practice: Size the pool from the database budget; keep blocking work off the event loop (use @Blocking or Mutiny offloading); set request body limits.

monitoring.signal: agroal pool gauges and vertx pool metrics

verification.criteria: db_pool and thread_pool settings are explicit.

entries.title: Fault tolerance annotations on remote calls
entries.requirement: Remote calls (REST client, messaging, database access to external systems) use MicroProfile Fault Tolerance annotations with explicit values, including timeouts on the REST client.
entries.best_practice: Set quarkus.rest-client connect and read timeouts; combine @Retry with jitter and a max duration; expose fault tolerance metrics.

monitoring.signal: ft.invocations.total, ft.circuitbreaker.state.current and ft.retry.calls.total

verification.criteria: Each remote dependency has a fault tolerance pattern.

entries.title: Graceful shutdown and start-up profile discipline
entries.requirement: A shutdown timeout is set for graceful draining, and production profile configuration disables Dev Services and dev-only endpoints.
entries.best_practice: Set quarkus.shutdown.timeout below the termination grace period; keep production settings in the %prod profile or injected environment; ensure OpenAPI and Swagger UI exposure is intentional.

monitoring.signal: errors during rollouts

verification.criteria: quarkus.shutdown.timeout is set and less than the grace period.

entries.title: Native-image versus JVM mode decision and memory sizing
entries.requirement: The runtime mode (JVM or native) is a deliberate decision, and memory requests and limits reflect it (native images need far less heap but different peak behaviour).
entries.best_practice: Load test the chosen mode; for JVM mode apply the Java heap sizing requirement; for native mode set explicit memory limits and watch RSS.

monitoring.signal: process memory and start-up time

verification.criteria: Memory limits match the runtime mode used by the image.

event_driven_messaging.title: Event-driven and messaging platforms
event_driven_messaging.description: Broker-agnostic requirements for event-driven services and messaging platforms (Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, JMS, Pulsar, cloud queues and topics).

entries.title: Idempotent consumers
entries.requirement: Message handlers tolerate duplicate and redelivered messages (at-least-once delivery) without repeating side effects.
entries.best_practice: Deduplicate on a message id or business key in the same transaction as the side effect; design operations to be naturally idempotent.
entries.audit_requirement: Processed message ids are retained for the deduplication window.

monitoring.signal: duplicate messages skipped
redelivery count

verification.criteria: Each messaging entry point shows an idempotency mechanism or idempotent effect.

entries.title: Dead-letter handling for poison messages
entries.requirement: Messages that fail repeatedly are moved to a dead-letter queue or topic after bounded retries, with the failure reason and original metadata, instead of blocking the partition or queue or being dropped.
entries.best_practice: Retry with backoff first; route to DLQ with headers describing the error; alert on DLQ depth; provide a replay tool with an owner and process.
entries.audit_requirement: Dead-lettered messages are retained and their handling is recorded.

monitoring.signal: dead-letter publish counter
DLQ depth and age of oldest message

verification.criteria: Each messaging entry point has a dead-letter or discard-with-record policy.

entries.title: Ordering, partitioning and concurrency chosen deliberately
entries.requirement: Where ordering matters, messages carry a key that routes related events to the same partition or queue consumer, and consumer concurrency does not exceed what ordering allows.
entries.best_practice: Key by aggregate id; document ordering guarantees; avoid parallelism inside a partition unless order is not needed.

monitoring.signal: per-partition or per-queue lag

verification.criteria: Message keys and concurrency settings are consistent with ordering needs.

entries.title: Backlog and age monitoring with alerts
entries.requirement: Queue depth or consumer lag and the age of the oldest unprocessed message are monitored with alerts tied to the processing SLO.
entries.best_practice: Alert on age (time to process) rather than raw depth; track per consumer group or subscription.

monitoring.signal: consumer lag and records consumed rate
monitoring.detail: client library metrics, not OneAgent defaults

monitoring.signal: broker-side lag and queue depth

verification.criteria: A telemetry library emitting consumer lag or queue depth is present and exported.

entries.title: Versioned, compatible message schemas
entries.requirement: Event payloads have a schema (Avro, Protobuf or JSON Schema) registered and evolved with compatibility checks, so producers and consumers deploy independently.
entries.best_practice: Use a schema registry with backward or full compatibility; include a version field; ignore unknown fields in consumers.
entries.audit_requirement: Schema change history retained.

monitoring.signal: deserialization error count

verification.criteria: A schema registry client or schema files exist.

entries.title: Reliable publication (outbox) for database plus message changes
entries.requirement: A state change and its event are published atomically (transactional outbox or change data capture), not with a dual write.
entries.best_practice: Write the event to an outbox table in the same transaction and relay it; or use CDC; make relays idempotent.

monitoring.signal: outbox backlog and publication delay

verification.criteria: Flows that write to a database and publish an event use an outbox or equivalent.

spring_boot_kafka.title: Spring Boot plus Kafka
spring_boot_kafka.description: Messaging requirements for Spring Boot services that produce or consume Kafka topics through Spring for Apache Kafka. Extends the event-driven baseline with consumer groups, dead letter topics and retry topics.

entry_extensions.kafka_property: the Kafka client or Spring property the requirement is expressed through

entries.title: Explicit and stable consumer group configuration
entries.requirement: Each listener has an explicit, stable group.id (never a generated one), a documented concurrency no greater than the partition count, and a cooperative assignment strategy where rebalances must be short.
entries.best_practice: Name groups after the service and function; use static membership (group.instance.id) for stateful consumers; set session.timeout.ms and heartbeat.interval.ms deliberately.
entries.audit_requirement: Consumer groups are registered with their owning team.

monitoring.signal: consumer rebalance rate and assigned partitions
consumer group state on the broker

verification.criteria: Every @KafkaListener sets a groupId or a default group id is configured, and concurrency is set.

entries.title: Offsets committed only after successful processing
entries.requirement: Auto-commit is off; offsets are committed by the listener container after the record is handled (record or batch ack mode), so failure never loses a message.
entries.best_practice: Use the container's ack-mode RECORD or BATCH with an error handler; commit after side effects; consider transactional processing for exactly-once between Kafka topics.

monitoring.signal: commit latency and commit rate
consumer lag

verification.criteria: enable.auto.commit is false and an ack mode is configured.

entries.title: Dead letter topic with bounded backoff
entries.requirement: The listener container error handler uses a bounded backoff (attempts and delays) and then publishes the record to a dead letter topic (DLT) with exception headers.
entries.best_practice: Use DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer with the same partition for ordering; classify non-retryable exceptions (validation, deserialization) to go straight to the DLT; give the DLT its own retention and an alert.
entries.audit_requirement: DLT records are retained for the investigation period.

monitoring.signal: records published to the DLT
DLT topic end offsets and consumer lag

verification.criteria: A dead letter recoverer or @RetryableTopic with a DLT is configured for each Kafka listener.

entries.title: Retry topics for non-blocking retries
entries.requirement: Retries with delay use retry topics (non-blocking) rather than blocking the partition with in-listener sleeps, with bounded attempts, increasing delay and a terminal DLT.
entries.best_practice: Use @RetryableTopic with exponential backoff and jitter; keep ordering-sensitive flows on blocking retry with a short bound; monitor each retry topic.

monitoring.signal: retry topic publish counts by attempt
retry topic lag

verification.criteria: Listeners that call fallible dependencies use retry topics or a bounded blocking backoff.

entries.title: Reliable producer settings
entries.requirement: Producers set acks=all, enable idempotence, and an explicit delivery timeout, with min.insync.replicas of at least 2 on the topic.
entries.best_practice: Handle send callbacks and failures; use a transactional producer where atomic multi-topic writes are needed; set linger and batch sizes from load tests.

monitoring.signal: record error rate and request latency

verification.criteria: Producer properties set acks, idempotence and delivery timeout.

entries.title: Poll settings match processing time
entries.requirement: max.poll.records and max.poll.interval.ms are set so the slowest batch finishes well before the poll interval, preventing spurious rebalances.
entries.best_practice: Reduce max.poll.records for slow handlers; move slow work off the poll thread only with careful ack handling; alert on rebalance frequency.

monitoring.signal: poll interval and rebalance rate

verification.criteria: Handler duration percentiles are below max.poll.interval.ms with margin.

entries.title: Poison-pill safe deserialization
entries.requirement: Deserializers are wrapped with ErrorHandlingDeserializer so a malformed record is routed to error handling rather than crashing the consumer in a loop.
entries.best_practice: Use a schema-aware deserializer with compatibility rules; restrict trusted packages for JSON type mapping.

monitoring.signal: deserialization error count

verification.criteria: ErrorHandlingDeserializer is configured for key and value deserialization.

entries.title: Kafka client metrics exported and alerted
entries.requirement: Consumer lag, records consumed per poll and commit latency are exported through Micrometer's Kafka metrics binding and alerted on.
entries.best_practice: Use the default Spring Boot Micrometer binding for Kafka consumer and producer metrics; alert on lag growth and on time-to-process.

monitoring.signal: kafka.consumer.fetch.manager.records.lag.max, records.consumed.total and commit.latency.avg

verification.criteria: A kafka_client telemetry library is detected and its metrics are exported.

oauth2_identity.title: OAuth2 identity
oauth2_identity.description: Requirements for services that authenticate with or through an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect identity provider, as a resource server, a client, or both.

entry_extensions.flow: the OAuth2 grant or role the requirement applies to (client_credentials, authorization_code, resource_server)

entries.title: Token refresh handled before expiry and safely under concurrency
entries.requirement: Clients cache access tokens and refresh them shortly before expiry (with clock-skew margin), refresh at most once concurrently (single flight), and handle refresh-token rotation and refresh failure without dropping requests.
entries.best_practice: Refresh proactively at around 80 percent of lifetime; retry refresh with bounded backoff; on refresh failure fall back to re-authentication and a circuit breaker; never log tokens.
entries.audit_requirement: Token issuance and refresh failures are logged with client id (not the token).

monitoring.signal: token refresh success, failure and latency counters
response time and failure rate of the token endpoint call

verification.criteria: An OAuth2 client library with token caching and refresh is used; the token endpoint is treated as a dependency with a timeout and a breaker.

entries.title: Credential rotation without downtime
entries.requirement: Client secrets or keys rotate on a schedule and after suspected leaks, with two credentials valid during the overlap, and services reload them without a redeploy.
entries.best_practice: Prefer private_key_jwt or mTLS client authentication over shared secrets; store credentials in a secrets manager; alert on credentials near expiry.
entries.audit_requirement: Rotation events and credential age are recorded and reviewed.

monitoring.signal: client credential age and expiry countdown
invalid_client errors after rotation

verification.criteria: Client credentials come from a secrets manager or vault and none are hardcoded.

entries.title: Resource server validates tokens completely
entries.requirement: Every protected endpoint validates the signature, issuer, audience, expiry and not-before of the access token, and enforces scopes or roles per operation.
entries.best_practice: Validate against the issuer's published keys (JWKS) with caching and key-rotation support; reject tokens with the wrong audience; map scopes to least-privilege permissions.
entries.audit_requirement: Authorization decisions for sensitive operations are logged with subject and scope.

monitoring.signal: authentication failures by reason
401 and 403 response rate

verification.criteria: Resource server configuration validates issuer and audience and every non-public route is secured.

entries.title: Identity provider outage tolerated
entries.requirement: Temporary unavailability of the identity provider does not fail already-authenticated traffic: JWKS keys are cached, token endpoint calls have timeouts and breakers, and cached tokens are used until expiry.
entries.best_practice: Refresh JWKS in the background with a stale-if-error window; set short timeouts on discovery and token calls.

monitoring.signal: availability of the identity provider service as seen by callers
JWKS refresh failures

verification.criteria: The identity provider dependency is classified and, if hard_failure, protected by caching or a fallback.

entries.title: Authorization code flow uses PKCE and secure redirect handling
entries.requirement: Public and browser-based clients use the authorization code flow with PKCE, exact-match redirect URIs and state validation; the implicit and password grants are not used.
entries.best_practice: Keep tokens out of URLs and local storage where possible; use short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens.

monitoring.signal: redirect URI mismatch and invalid state events

verification.criteria: Client registration and code use authorization code with PKCE only.

entries.title: Token and session revocation
entries.requirement: Logout and account compromise revoke sessions and refresh tokens, and access tokens are short-lived enough that revocation takes effect within the accepted window.
entries.best_practice: Use token revocation and introspection for high-risk operations; back-channel logout for federated sessions.
entries.audit_requirement: Revocations are recorded with the reason.

monitoring.signal: revocation and logout events

verification.criteria: Revocation paths exist and access token lifetime is documented.

jwt_authentication.title: JWT authentication
jwt_authentication.description: Requirements for services that issue or accept JSON Web Tokens directly (signed JWT bearer tokens, service-issued session tokens).

entries.title: Signature algorithm allow-list and strong keys
entries.requirement: Only an explicit allow-list of asymmetric algorithms (for example RS256, ES256) is accepted; none and algorithm downgrade are rejected; symmetric keys, where used, are long random values from a secrets store.
entries.best_practice: Pin the algorithm per issuer; never let the token header choose; use at least 2048-bit RSA or P-256 keys.
entries.audit_requirement: Key generation and storage follow the key management policy.

monitoring.signal: rejected tokens by reason (algorithm, signature)

verification.criteria: Verification is configured with a fixed algorithm and no signing key is hardcoded.

entries.title: Complete claim validation
entries.requirement: Every token is validated for issuer, audience, expiry and not-before with a small clock-skew allowance, and required claims are present.
entries.best_practice: Reject tokens missing exp; keep skew to a minute or less; validate the subject against the expected type.

monitoring.signal: 401 response rate

verification.criteria: Validation code checks iss, aud, exp and nbf.

entries.title: Short lifetimes and key rotation with kid
entries.requirement: Access tokens are short-lived, signing keys rotate on a schedule, and tokens carry a key id (kid) so verifiers pick the right key during rotation.
entries.best_practice: Publish keys through a JWKS endpoint with cache headers; overlap old and new keys; keep access token lifetime at minutes.
entries.audit_requirement: Key rotation history retained.

monitoring.signal: signing key age
unknown kid failures

verification.criteria: Token lifetime and rotation schedule are documented and implemented.

entries.title: No sensitive data in token payloads and bounded token size
entries.requirement: Token payloads carry only identifiers and needed claims (no secrets or unnecessary personal data), and token size is bounded to avoid header size failures.
entries.best_practice: JWTs are signed, not encrypted, unless JWE is used; keep claims minimal; look up details server-side.
entries.audit_requirement: Claim set is reviewed for personal data.

monitoring.signal: 431 and 400 response rate from oversized headers

verification.criteria: Claims listed contain no secrets or unnecessary personal data.

zero_trust.title: Zero trust
zero_trust.description: Requirements for services operating under a zero trust model: no implicit trust from network location, strong workload identity, and per-request authorisation.

entries.title: Every service-to-service call is authenticated with workload identity
entries.requirement: Calls between services authenticate the calling workload (mTLS with mesh or SPIFFE identities, or signed workload tokens) rather than trusting the network path.
entries.best_practice: Issue short-lived identities automatically; enforce strict mTLS in the mesh; map identities to services, not IP ranges.
entries.audit_requirement: Workload identity issuance and denied connections are logged.

monitoring.signal: mTLS coverage percentage and denied connection count

verification.criteria: mTLS is enforced in strict mode for the service's namespace or mesh.

entries.title: Default-deny network and authorisation policies
entries.requirement: Network policies and mesh authorisation policies deny all traffic by default and allow only the required source, destination and operation.
entries.best_practice: Apply a default-deny NetworkPolicy per namespace; write allow rules per service pair; use AuthorizationPolicy with principals and paths, not just ports.
entries.audit_requirement: Policy changes are version controlled and reviewed.

monitoring.signal: denied flows and policy change events

verification.criteria: At least one default-deny NetworkPolicy or AuthorizationPolicy covers the workload; namespaces with none are a finding.

entries.title: Per-request authorisation at every service
entries.requirement: Each service authorises each request against the caller's identity and the operation, and does not assume a request is trusted because it came from an internal service or gateway.
entries.best_practice: Propagate the end-user identity token (or a signed context) to downstream services; enforce least-privilege scopes; centralise policy where possible.
entries.audit_requirement: Authorisation decisions on sensitive operations are logged.

monitoring.signal: 401 and 403 response rate per service

verification.criteria: A security library is a dependency and entry points are protected.

entries.title: Short-lived, least-privilege credentials
entries.requirement: Workloads use short-lived credentials obtained through workload identity, scoped to the minimum permissions, with no long-lived shared secrets between services.
entries.best_practice: Use platform workload identity federation; rotate automatically; review permissions regularly.
entries.audit_requirement: Credential and permission reviews are recorded.

monitoring.signal: credential age and permission usage

verification.criteria: Workloads use a dedicated service account and no static shared credentials.

entries.title: Continuous verification and telemetry of access
entries.requirement: Access decisions and anomalies (unusual callers, failed authentication bursts) are logged centrally and monitored, so trust is verified continuously rather than granted once.
entries.best_practice: Centralise audit logs; alert on new caller identities and denied-request spikes.
entries.audit_requirement: Access logs retained per policy.

monitoring.signal: authentication and authorisation events by principal
service call topology changes

verification.criteria: Security events are collected and alerted on.

source_github.title: GitHub source control and Actions
source_github.description: Requirements for repositories hosted on GitHub, including GitHub Actions workflows.

entries.title: Protected default branch with required review and checks
entries.requirement: The default and release branches are protected: pull request required, at least one approving review (code owners for sensitive paths), required status checks, no force pushes or deletions.
entries.best_practice: Use CODEOWNERS; require branches to be up to date; require signed commits where policy demands.
entries.audit_requirement: Branch protection settings and bypass events are retained in the audit log.

monitoring.signal: GitHub audit log events for branch protection changes and bypasses

verification.criteria: Branch protection is enabled on the default branch (repository settings) and a CI workflow provides the required checks.

entries.title: Secret scanning and push protection enabled
entries.requirement: Secret scanning and push protection are enabled so credentials cannot be committed, and dependency alerts (Dependabot or equivalent) are enabled and triaged.
entries.best_practice: Enable code scanning and dependency review on pull requests; block on high-severity findings.
entries.audit_requirement: Alert triage history retained.

monitoring.signal: open secret scanning and dependency alerts by age

verification.criteria: Repository security features are enabled and no committed secrets remain.

entries.title: Least-privilege workflow permissions and pinned actions
entries.requirement: Workflows set explicit minimal permissions (read-only contents by default), third-party actions are pinned to a commit SHA, and untrusted pull request input is never executed with secrets.
entries.best_practice: Set permissions at workflow or job level; avoid pull_request_target with checkout of untrusted code; review action updates.

monitoring.signal: workflow runs by trigger and permission scope

verification.criteria: Workflow files declare permissions and pin actions by SHA.

entries.title: Deployments use environments and short-lived cloud credentials
entries.requirement: Production deployment jobs use GitHub environments with required reviewers, and authenticate to the cloud through OIDC federation instead of long-lived stored credentials.
entries.best_practice: Restrict environment secrets to the deploy job; use deployment protection rules; record the deployed commit.
entries.audit_requirement: Deployment approvals are retained.

monitoring.signal: deployment history per environment

verification.criteria: Deploying workflows reference an environment and use OIDC.

entries.title: Build reproducibility and artifact provenance
entries.requirement: Builds are reproducible from a commit, artifacts are versioned and traceable (SBOM, provenance attestation), and the same artifact is promoted through environments.
entries.best_practice: Generate an SBOM and provenance in CI; sign images; store artifacts in a registry with retention rules.
entries.audit_requirement: SBOM and provenance retained per release.

monitoring.signal: attestation and signature verification results at deploy time

verification.criteria: Provenance or SBOM steps exist in the pipeline.

cicd_harness.title: Harness CI/CD
cicd_harness.description: Requirements for delivery pipelines defined in Harness (pipelines, stages, step groups, templates, delegates).

entry_extensions.harness_construct: the Harness object the requirement is expressed through (strategy, failureStrategies, rollbackSteps, ...)

entries.title: Deployment stages use a progressive strategy
entries.requirement: Production deploy stages use a Harness Canary, Blue-Green or Rolling execution strategy with phased steps, not a bare apply of all instances.
entries.best_practice: Use canary phases with a verification step between them; keep rolling batch size small for user-facing services.
entries.audit_requirement: Pipeline execution records (who, what, when) are retained.

monitoring.signal: pipeline execution status and phase durations
error rate and response time during phases

verification.criteria: Harness pipelines that deploy show a canary, blue_green or rolling deployment_strategy.

entries.title: Rollback steps and failure strategies defined
entries.requirement: Each deploy stage defines rollbackSteps and a failure strategy (rollback stage on failure or verification failure), so a failed step reverts automatically, or a manual rollback pipeline is documented.
entries.best_practice: Use automatic rollback on verification failure; keep a separate tested rollback pipeline for post-release regressions.
entries.audit_requirement: Rollback executions record the trigger and approver.

monitoring.signal: rollback executions per service

verification.criteria: rollback.mode is automated or manual for Harness pipelines that deploy.

entries.title: Continuous verification against monitoring
entries.requirement: Deploy stages include a verification step using the monitoring provider (for example Dynatrace) that compares the new version against the baseline before completing the rollout.
entries.best_practice: Verify error rate, latency and saturation for a defined window; fail the stage on regression so rollback triggers.
entries.audit_requirement: Verification results are stored with the execution.

monitoring.signal: service failure rate and response time for old and new versions

verification.criteria: A verification step appears between deployment and completion.

entries.harness_construct: Verify step with the monitoring provider

entries.title: Database migrations as a separate, approved step
entries.requirement: Schema migration runs in its own stage or step before the application deploy, with approval where policy requires, and the pipeline halts on migration failure.
entries.best_practice: Run migrations from a versioned image or job; keep the deploy stage dependent on migration success.
entries.audit_requirement: Migration executions and approvals retained.

monitoring.signal: migration step outcome and duration

verification.criteria: When a migration tool is present, separate_step is true.

entries.harness_construct: dedicated migration step or stage with approval

entries.title: Secrets through Harness secret managers and governed templates
entries.requirement: Pipelines read credentials from a Harness secret manager (Vault, GCP Secret Manager or similar) by reference, use shared templates for deploy stages, and are governed by policy (OPA) checks.
entries.best_practice: Scope secrets to projects; use step templates for security scans; keep delegates highly available and least-privileged.
entries.audit_requirement: Harness audit trail is retained and exported.

monitoring.signal: delegate health and pipeline policy evaluation failures

verification.criteria: No literal credentials in pipeline YAML; secrets are referenced through a secret manager.

entries.harness_construct: secretManager references, pipeline templates, OPA policies

cicd_ucd.title: UrbanCode Deploy (UCD)
cicd_ucd.description: Requirements for deployments driven by IBM UrbanCode Deploy application, component and generic processes. Applies where UCD is used.

entries.title: Deployment and rollback processes are both defined
entries.requirement: Each application has an application process for deployment and a tested application process for rollback (redeploying the previous snapshot), and the deploy process handles failure by invoking or preparing rollback.
entries.best_practice: Use component version snapshots for whole-application rollback; rehearse rollback in a lower environment.
entries.audit_requirement: Every deployment and rollback request is recorded with requester and approver.

monitoring.signal: process execution results per environment

verification.criteria: A rollback process exists for each deployment process (rollback.mode is not none_defined).

entries.title: Environment approvals and gates
entries.requirement: Production environments require approval processes and pass configured gates (tests, change ticket) before deployment.
entries.best_practice: Use environment gates; restrict who can deploy to production by role; separate duties between requester and approver.
entries.audit_requirement: Approval history is retained per deployment.

monitoring.signal: approvals pending and gate results

verification.criteria: Approval and gate steps are defined for production.

entries.title: Versioned snapshots and immutable component versions
entries.requirement: Deployments reference component versions and snapshots that are immutable and traceable to a build; latest or floating versions are not deployed to production.
entries.best_practice: Create a snapshot per release candidate; promote the same snapshot through environments.
entries.audit_requirement: Snapshot to commit traceability retained.

monitoring.signal: deployed version per environment

verification.criteria: Production deployments reference snapshots, not floating versions.

entries.title: Sensitive properties secured and agents highly available
entries.requirement: Passwords and tokens in process properties are stored as secure properties (or from a vault plug-in), and UCD agents and servers used for production run with redundancy.
entries.best_practice: Mask secure properties in logs; use agent relays and at least two agents for critical deployment paths.
entries.audit_requirement: Access to secure properties is audited.

monitoring.signal: agent online status

verification.criteria: No literal credentials appear in UCD process definitions.

entries.title: Database changes as separate processes
entries.requirement: Database schema changes run as their own component process with approval, executed before the application component, not embedded in the application start-up.
entries.best_practice: Keep database change scripts versioned as components; run a compatibility check before the application step.
entries.audit_requirement: Schema change executions retained.

monitoring.signal: database component process results

verification.criteria: Migration steps are separate processes when present.

iac_terraform.title: Terraform
iac_terraform.description: Requirements for infrastructure defined as code with Terraform (any provider), including Google Cloud resources.

entries.title: Remote, locked and encrypted state
entries.requirement: State is stored in a remote backend with locking, encryption at rest, versioning and restricted access, never committed to the repository.
entries.best_practice: Use a bucket backend with versioning and a lock mechanism; separate state per environment and component; restrict who can read state (it can contain secrets).
entries.audit_requirement: State access and changes are logged.

monitoring.signal: backend access logs and state lock events

verification.criteria: Backend configuration is remote with locking; no state file is committed.

entries.title: Pinned provider and module versions
entries.requirement: Terraform, provider and module versions are pinned with version constraints and a committed dependency lock file.
entries.best_practice: Use required_version and required_providers with constraints; update through reviewed pull requests; pin module sources to tags or commits.

monitoring.signal: drift between planned and applied provider versions

verification.criteria: required_providers has version constraints and .terraform.lock.hcl is committed.

entries.title: Plan review and policy checks before apply
entries.requirement: Every change is planned, reviewed and checked by policy tooling (for example Checkov, tfsec, OPA or Sentinel) before apply, and applied through a pipeline, not from workstations.
entries.best_practice: Post the plan on the pull request; fail on high-severity policy findings; require approval for production applies.
entries.audit_requirement: Plans, approvals and applies are retained.

monitoring.signal: apply outcomes and policy check results

verification.criteria: A pipeline runs plan, policy check and gated apply.

entries.title: No secrets in code, variables or outputs
entries.requirement: Secrets are not in .tf or .tfvars files; sensitive variables and outputs are marked sensitive, and secret values are read from a secrets manager at apply time or referenced by the resource.
entries.best_practice: Use data sources for secrets; generate credentials in the platform where possible; treat state as sensitive.

monitoring.signal: secret scanning results on Terraform files

verification.criteria: No hardcoded credential findings with location_type iac.

entries.title: Stateful resources protected from accidental destruction
entries.requirement: Databases, disks, buckets and keys have deletion protection and lifecycle prevent_destroy, backups enabled, and encryption configured in the resource definition.
entries.best_practice: Use deletion_protection where the provider offers it; require explicit approval for destroy plans; tag resources with owner and environment.
entries.audit_requirement: Destroy operations on stateful resources are approved and recorded.

monitoring.signal: resource deletion events in cloud audit logs

verification.criteria: Stateful resource types define deletion protection, backup and encryption attributes.

entries.title: Drift detection and environment separation
entries.requirement: Deployed infrastructure is compared with code on a schedule, and environments are separated by state and credentials, not by workspaces alone.
entries.best_practice: Run scheduled plans and alert on drift; use separate projects or accounts per environment; keep modules generic and environment values in variables.

monitoring.signal: scheduled plan drift reports

verification.criteria: Drift detection exists and environments are isolated.

docker.title: Docker and container images
docker.description: Requirements for container images and Docker Compose definitions.

entries.title: Images run as a non-root user
entries.requirement: Each image sets a non-root USER (numeric) and does not require privileged mode or added capabilities.
entries.best_practice: Create a dedicated user; drop all Linux capabilities and add back only what is needed; use a read-only root filesystem where the application allows.

monitoring.signal: admission or runtime policy violations for root containers

verification.criteria: Every Dockerfile sets a non-root user and no workload runs as root.

entries.title: Minimal, pinned base images and multi-stage builds
entries.requirement: Base images are minimal (slim, distroless or similar), pinned to a specific version or digest (never latest), and the build uses multi-stage builds so build tools are not in the runtime image.
entries.best_practice: Rebuild regularly to pick up patches; scan images in CI and in the registry; keep the image small.
entries.audit_requirement: Image scan results retained per release.

monitoring.signal: image vulnerabilities by severity in the registry

verification.criteria: Base images carry explicit version tags or digests and none uses the latest tag.

entries.title: Health check defined where no orchestrator probe applies
entries.requirement: Images or Compose services define a HEALTHCHECK (or an orchestrator probe) so a hung process is detected and restarted.
entries.best_practice: Use a lightweight check against the readiness endpoint; set interval, timeout and retries; use depends_on with a healthy condition for start order.

monitoring.signal: container health status and restart count

verification.criteria: Each Dockerfile or Compose service has a health check or is orchestrated with probes; Compose services have a restart policy.

entries.title: No secrets baked into image layers or Compose files
entries.requirement: Images and Compose files contain no credentials, keys or tokens; build secrets use BuildKit secret mounts and runtime secrets are injected.
entries.best_practice: Use .dockerignore; use secret mounts for build-time credentials; scan images for embedded secrets.

monitoring.signal: secret scanning results on images and repositories

verification.criteria: No hardcoded credential findings in Dockerfiles or Compose files (demo defaults are noted).

entries.title: Resource limits and signal handling
entries.requirement: Compose services set memory and CPU limits, and images run the application as PID 1 through an init or exec form so SIGTERM reaches it and shutdown is graceful.
entries.best_practice: Use exec form ENTRYPOINT or tini; set stop_grace_period; set limits under deploy.resources or the runtime's flags.

monitoring.signal: container CPU and memory usage

verification.criteria: Compose services declare limits.

kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
kubernetes.description: Platform-specific requirements for workloads on Kubernetes (including Helm-rendered manifests and GKE). Resource sizing, autoscaling, replicas and rollout are cross-cutting requirements evaluated in the capacity and deployment modules.

entries.title: Liveness, readiness and startup probes of the right kind
entries.requirement: Each container has a readiness probe, a liveness probe that does not depend on downstream services, and a startup probe for slow-starting applications, each with explicit thresholds and timeouts.
entries.best_practice: Use HTTP probes against dedicated endpoints; set initialDelay only when a startup probe is not used; avoid probes that call databases.

monitoring.signal: probe failures and container restarts

verification.criteria: All three probe types are set appropriately for each container; missing probes are findings.

entries.title: Hardened security context
entries.requirement: Pods run as non-root with a read-only root filesystem where possible, privilege escalation disabled and all capabilities dropped, under a Pod Security Standard of at least baseline (restricted for new workloads).
entries.best_practice: Set runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, capabilities drop ALL and seccomp RuntimeDefault; enforce with Pod Security Admission.
entries.audit_requirement: Policy violations are logged.

monitoring.signal: admission denials and policy violations

verification.criteria: Containers set run_as_non_root true and use a dedicated service account.

entries.title: Network policies restrict traffic
entries.requirement: Each namespace has a default-deny NetworkPolicy with explicit allow rules for the service's required ingress and egress.
entries.best_practice: Allow only DNS, the required dependencies and the ingress controller; label workloads consistently for selectors.
entries.audit_requirement: Policy changes reviewed via version control.

monitoring.signal: dropped connections by policy

verification.criteria: NetworkPolicy resources exist covering the workload namespace.

entries.title: Failure-domain spreading and disruption protection
entries.requirement: Multi-replica workloads spread across nodes and zones with topology spread constraints or anti-affinity, and are protected by a PodDisruptionBudget.
entries.best_practice: Use topologySpreadConstraints with maxSkew 1 across zones and hostnames; combine with a PDB.

monitoring.signal: replica distribution across nodes and zones

verification.criteria: Workloads with two or more replicas have spread constraints and a budget.

entries.title: Namespace quotas and default limits
entries.requirement: Namespaces define ResourceQuota and LimitRange so no workload can consume unbounded resources or run without requests and limits.
entries.best_practice: Set quotas per team and environment; set LimitRange defaults; monitor quota usage.
