monitoring.signal: quota utilisation by namespace

verification.criteria: Quotas exist for the workload's namespace.

entries.title: Ingress and services expose only what is needed with TLS
entries.requirement: Only the intended services are exposed (ClusterIP by default, LoadBalancer or NodePort only when required), and ingresses terminate TLS with managed certificates.
entries.best_practice: Use one ingress controller with TLS everywhere; do not use NodePort in production; restrict the management port.

monitoring.signal: certificate expiry and ingress error rate

verification.criteria: No unneeded NodePort or LoadBalancer services and every ingress host has TLS.

entries.title: Kubernetes API audit logging and RBAC least privilege
entries.requirement: The cluster records API audit logs (including secret access and exec) and workloads use RBAC roles limited to what they need, with service account token automounting disabled unless required.
entries.best_practice: Ship audit logs to central storage with retention; review cluster-admin bindings; disable automount for workloads that do not call the API.
entries.audit_requirement: Audit logs retained per policy and reviewed.

monitoring.signal: audit events for exec, secret get and RBAC changes

verification.criteria: Audit logging is enabled on the cluster and workloads use non-default service accounts.

openshift.title: OpenShift
openshift.description: Requirements specific to Red Hat OpenShift, in addition to the Kubernetes module. Applies where OpenShift resources (DeploymentConfig, Route, ImageStream) or oc-based deployment steps are found.

entries.title: Workloads compatible with the restricted security context constraint
entries.requirement: Applications run under the restricted (or restricted-v2) SCC with an arbitrary non-root UID, not a custom SCC with elevated privileges, and images do not depend on a fixed UID or writable root paths.
entries.best_practice: Make writable directories group-writable for GID 0; avoid anyuid and privileged SCCs; review any SCC grants to service accounts.
entries.audit_requirement: SCC grants are reviewed and recorded.

monitoring.signal: pods rejected by SCC admission

verification.criteria: No workload requires an elevated SCC.

entries.title: Routes use TLS with redirect and appropriate termination
entries.requirement: Routes terminate TLS (edge or re-encrypt for sensitive traffic, passthrough where end-to-end TLS is required) and redirect insecure traffic, with certificates managed centrally.
entries.best_practice: Use insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy Redirect; re-encrypt to the pod for sensitive data; avoid unencrypted routes.

monitoring.signal: router error rate and certificate expiry

verification.criteria: Every route or ingress host has TLS.

entries.title: Deployment resources use Deployment, not deprecated DeploymentConfig
entries.requirement: New workloads use Deployment objects with the standard rollout strategy; existing DeploymentConfigs have a migration plan, since DeploymentConfig is deprecated.
entries.best_practice: Migrate to Deployment with rolling or recreate strategy and ImageStream tag triggers where needed.

monitoring.signal: rollout status per workload

verification.criteria: Workload kinds are Deployment or StatefulSet; DeploymentConfig is a finding.

entries.title: Project quotas, image provenance and rollback tooling
entries.requirement: Projects have quotas and limit ranges, images come from trusted registries or ImageStreams with pinned tags or digests, and rollback is possible through oc rollout undo or a redeploy of the previous image.
entries.best_practice: Use ImageStream tags per release; enable image signature verification; monitor project quota use.
entries.audit_requirement: Image import and deployment history retained.

monitoring.signal: project quota usage and image import failures

verification.criteria: Images are pinned and a rollback path exists.

rest_apis.title: REST APIs
rest_apis.description: Requirements for HTTP/REST interfaces the service exposes (and, where relevant, the way it calls others).

entries.title: Consistent error model and correct status codes
entries.requirement: Errors are returned with correct HTTP status codes and a consistent machine-readable body (for example RFC 9457 problem details), with no stack traces or internal details.
entries.best_practice: Map domain errors to 4xx and infrastructure failures to 5xx; include a correlation id; never leak exception messages.

monitoring.signal: HTTP 4xx and 5xx response rate by request

verification.criteria: Error handling is centralised and returns problem-style bodies.

entries.title: Input validation and request size limits
entries.requirement: Every entry point validates input (types, ranges, required fields) and enforces limits on request body size, pagination page size and query complexity.
entries.best_practice: Use declarative validation; cap page sizes; reject oversized bodies at the gateway or server.
entries.audit_requirement: Rejected malformed requests are counted and reviewed for abuse patterns.

monitoring.signal: 400 and 413 response rate

verification.criteria: Validation annotations or schemas exist for write endpoints and list endpoints are paginated.

entries.title: Idempotent methods and idempotency keys for creation
entries.requirement: GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent, and POST endpoints that create resources or trigger payments accept an idempotency key.
entries.best_practice: Store the key with the result for a TTL and return the stored result on repeat; never mutate on GET.
entries.audit_requirement: Idempotency keys recorded with financial writes.

monitoring.signal: idempotent replays served

verification.criteria: GET entry points show no writes in the flow steps; creation endpoints handle repeated submissions.

entries.title: Published, versioned contract with compatibility tests
entries.requirement: The API has a published contract (OpenAPI), a versioning scheme, and consumer or contract tests that fail the build on breaking changes.
entries.best_practice: Generate the contract from code or code from the contract; deprecate with Sunset headers and telemetry on usage.
entries.audit_requirement: Contract change history retained.

monitoring.signal: requests per API version

verification.criteria: An OpenAPI document exists and contract tests run in CI.

entries.title: Rate limiting, timeouts and safe caching headers
entries.requirement: Public endpoints have rate limits and request timeouts, and responses set caching headers (Cache-Control, ETag) deliberately, with no caching of personalised or sensitive responses.
entries.best_practice: Return 429 with Retry-After; set no-store on sensitive responses; use conditional requests for read-heavy resources.

monitoring.signal: 429 response rate and response size

verification.criteria: Rate limiting exists in application, gateway or mesh and headers are set on sensitive responses.

entries.title: Health, readiness and version endpoints separate from business API
entries.requirement: Health and info endpoints are served separately from the business API (own path or port), are unauthenticated only for the platform, and do not expose sensitive details.
entries.best_practice: Return a version and build id for troubleshooting; keep health responses minimal.

monitoring.signal: probe results

verification.criteria: Probes use dedicated paths.

api_gateway.title: API gateways
api_gateway.description: Requirements for the API gateway layer (Apigee, Kong, Spring Cloud Gateway, cloud API gateways, ingress gateways acting as API gateways).

entries.title: Centralised authentication and coarse authorisation at the edge
entries.requirement: The gateway authenticates callers (validating tokens or API keys) and enforces coarse authorisation, while backends still enforce fine-grained authorisation.
entries.best_practice: Validate JWTs at the gateway with cached keys; strip and re-issue identity headers; never trust client-set identity headers.
entries.audit_requirement: Authentication decisions are logged at the gateway.

monitoring.signal: gateway 401 and 403 rate by consumer

verification.criteria: Gateway policy validates tokens and backends re-check authorisation.

entries.title: Rate limits, quotas, size limits and timeouts at the edge
entries.requirement: The gateway enforces per-consumer rate limits and quotas, maximum request and response sizes, and upstream timeouts.
entries.best_practice: Differentiate limits by consumer tier; fail with 429 and Retry-After; set gateway timeouts above backend timeouts by a small margin.

monitoring.signal: throttled requests and upstream timeout counts

verification.criteria: Rate limiting and timeout policies are present in gateway configuration.

entries.title: Gateway retries and circuit breaking are safe
entries.requirement: The gateway retries only idempotent requests, with bounded attempts, and uses upstream health checks or circuit breaking so failed backends are ejected quickly; retries are not duplicated by the backend or mesh.
entries.best_practice: Decide one layer to own retries; use outlier detection; configure retry budgets.

monitoring.signal: upstream retry and ejection counts

verification.criteria: Retry ownership across gateway, mesh and application is documented and non-duplicating.

entries.title: Gateway is highly available and scales
entries.requirement: The gateway runs redundantly across zones with autoscaling, and its configuration is deployed as code with staged rollout.
entries.best_practice: Treat the gateway as a critical hard dependency for all callers; test failover; keep configuration in version control.
entries.audit_requirement: Gateway configuration changes are versioned and attributable.

monitoring.signal: gateway availability, latency and saturation
gateway process availability where OneAgent monitors it

verification.criteria: Gateway workloads have at least two replicas and autoscaling, or a managed HA gateway is used.

entries.title: TLS termination, WAF and access logging
entries.requirement: The gateway terminates TLS with modern policy, applies web application firewall protections where required, and writes access logs with correlation ids.
entries.best_practice: Use managed certificates; enable OWASP rule sets in detection then blocking mode; ship access logs centrally.
entries.audit_requirement: Gateway access logs retained per policy.

monitoring.signal: gateway access logs and blocked request events

verification.criteria: TLS policy, WAF and access logs are configured.

service_mesh.title: Service mesh
service_mesh.description: Requirements for services running in a service mesh (Istio, Linkerd or equivalent).

entries.title: Strict mTLS between meshed services
entries.requirement: mTLS is enforced in strict mode for the service's namespace or the whole mesh, not left permissive.
entries.best_practice: Use a mesh-wide PeerAuthentication STRICT (Istio) or default Linkerd mTLS; migrate through permissive mode with a deadline; monitor plaintext traffic.
entries.audit_requirement: mTLS policy is version controlled.

monitoring.signal: percentage of meshed traffic using mTLS

verification.criteria: mtls mode is strict for the service scope; permissive or missing is a finding.

entries.title: Retry and timeout policy owned by the mesh without duplication
entries.requirement: Retries and timeouts for each service call are defined at the mesh layer or the application, not multiplied across both, with bounded attempts and per-try timeouts.
entries.best_practice: Use VirtualService retries with retryOn limited to safe conditions; set overall timeout above per-try timeout times attempts; document ownership.

monitoring.signal: proxy upstream retry counts and timeouts

verification.criteria: Each dependency has retry and timeout at exactly one layer (resilience_by_layer cross reference).

entries.title: Circuit breaking and outlier detection for upstreams
entries.requirement: Destination rules define connection pool limits and outlier detection (ejection after consecutive errors) for critical upstreams.
entries.best_practice: Tune maxConnections and pending requests from load tests; set base ejection time and max ejection percent to avoid ejecting the whole pool.

monitoring.signal: outlier ejections and overflow counters

verification.criteria: circuit_breaker and connection_pool policies exist for hard_failure dependencies.

entries.title: Default-deny authorisation policy
entries.requirement: Authorisation policies deny by default and allow specific service identities, methods and paths.
entries.best_practice: Start with a namespace-wide deny-all AuthorizationPolicy and add allows per caller; audit policy hits.
entries.audit_requirement: Policy changes are reviewed.

monitoring.signal: denied requests by policy

verification.criteria: Authorization policies exist for the service.

entries.title: Sidecar and control plane resilience
entries.requirement: Sidecar proxies have resource requests and limits and start before the application; the control plane is highly available and upgraded in a controlled way, and data plane traffic continues if it is unavailable.
entries.best_practice: Use holdApplicationUntilProxyStarts; run multiple control plane replicas; canary control plane upgrades.

monitoring.signal: control plane health and proxy sync status

verification.criteria: Injection is enabled and sidecar resources are bounded.

data_relational.title: Relational databases (general)
data_relational.description: Engine-independent requirements for services using relational databases (JDBC, ORM, SQL drivers). Engine-specific modules extend this one.

entries.title: Production uses a durable database, not an embedded or in-memory one
entries.requirement: Production profiles connect to a managed or clustered relational database with persistence; embedded databases such as H2, HSQLDB or SQLite in-memory are for local development and tests only.
entries.best_practice: Select the datasource per profile; keep the same engine in CI as in production (for example Testcontainers); never let the default in-memory profile reach production.

monitoring.signal: database service detected for the calling service
monitoring.detail: the connected database type and host are visible

verification.criteria: A production-grade driver and database workload or managed instance exist; H2 or another embedded database is present only for local profiles.

entries.title: Explicit connection pool, transaction and statement timeouts
entries.requirement: The pool size, connection acquisition timeout, idle and lifetime limits, and statement, lock and transaction timeouts are set explicitly, and transactions are as short as possible.
entries.best_practice: Set statement and lock timeouts at the database role or driver level; use read-only transactions for queries; avoid holding a transaction across remote calls.

monitoring.signal: pool active, pending, timeout and usage metrics
database call response time and failure rate

verification.criteria: db_pool settings are explicit and a timeout pattern covers datastore calls.

entries.title: Versioned schema migrations
entries.requirement: Schema changes are managed with a migration tool (Flyway, Liquibase, Alembic or equivalent) with versioned, reviewed scripts; the application does not auto-alter production schemas.
entries.best_practice: Keep scripts immutable once released; test migrations against a production-like copy; run them as a separate step.
entries.audit_requirement: Migration history table and scripts retained.

monitoring.signal: migration execution log

verification.criteria: A schema_migration dependency exists or scripts are managed by a pipeline step; schema is not auto-created in production.

entries.title: Backups, restore tests and recovery objectives
entries.requirement: Databases are backed up automatically with point-in-time recovery where the engine supports it, restores are tested on a schedule, and RPO and RTO are defined and met.
entries.best_practice: Store backups in a separate failure domain, encrypted; automate restore drills; alert on backup failure.
entries.audit_requirement: Backup success and restore test evidence retained.

monitoring.signal: backup success, age of last backup and restore test results

verification.criteria: Backup configuration is present in infrastructure code or platform settings and a restore has been tested.

entries.title: Replication and failover for the primary
entries.requirement: The primary database has a replica or managed high-availability failover, and the application reconnects automatically after failover.
entries.best_practice: Connect through a stable endpoint; validate connections on borrow; test failover; route read-only work to replicas where suitable.

monitoring.signal: replication lag and failover events
database call failure rate during failover

verification.criteria: A single-instance database in production is a finding; managed HA or replication is present.

entries.title: Parameterised queries and least-privilege accounts
entries.requirement: All queries use bound parameters (no string-built SQL from input), and the application connects with an account limited to the privileges it needs, separate from the migration and admin accounts.
entries.best_practice: Use ORM or prepared statements; separate roles for migration and runtime; rotate credentials.
entries.audit_requirement: Database privileges are reviewed periodically.

monitoring.signal: database audit of privileged statements

verification.criteria: Queries are parameterised and the application account does not have admin privileges.

entries.title: Query performance visibility
entries.requirement: Slow queries, N+1 access patterns and missing indexes are detectable through statement-level monitoring, and critical queries have reviewed execution plans and indexes.
entries.best_practice: Use statement-level tracing from the observability platform and the engine's slow query log; review plans in code review for new queries.

monitoring.signal: database statements per request with response time
slow query log and index usage statistics

verification.criteria: Slow statements are visible per calling service and reviewed.

data_postgres.title: PostgreSQL
data_postgres.description: PostgreSQL-specific requirements, extending the general relational database module.

entry_extensions.pg_setting: the PostgreSQL setting or driver property the requirement is expressed through

entries.title: Connection budget and pooling
entries.requirement: The total connections from all replicas at maximum scale stay within max_connections minus reserved superuser connections, using an external pooler (PgBouncer, or a managed pooler) when replicas times pool size would exceed it.
entries.best_practice: Prefer transaction pooling for many small clients (mind prepared statements and session state); monitor connection saturation.

monitoring.signal: active connections versus max_connections
application pool active and pending connections

verification.criteria: pool size multiplied by maximum replicas is below max_connections.

entries.title: TLS with certificate verification
entries.requirement: Client connections use TLS with server certificate verification (verify-full), and the server rejects non-TLS connections through pg_hba hostssl rules.
entries.best_practice: Distribute the CA certificate through a secret or trust store; use IAM or certificate authentication where available.

monitoring.signal: sessions by SSL status from pg_stat_ssl

verification.criteria: JDBC or driver URLs enable ssl with verify-full.

entries.title: Statement, lock and idle-in-transaction timeouts
entries.requirement: statement_timeout, lock_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout are set for the application role so runaway queries, lock waits and abandoned transactions cannot hold resources indefinitely.
entries.best_practice: Set per role with ALTER ROLE; use lower values for OLTP roles than for reporting roles.

monitoring.signal: long-running queries and idle in transaction sessions from pg_stat_activity

verification.criteria: Role-level timeouts are configured.

entries.title: Backups with point-in-time recovery and tested restore
entries.requirement: Continuous WAL archiving or managed automated backups provide point-in-time recovery inside the RPO, and restores are tested.
entries.best_practice: Use the managed service's PITR; retain backups per policy; monitor archive lag.
entries.audit_requirement: Restore test results retained.

monitoring.signal: WAL archive lag and last successful backup

verification.criteria: Backup and PITR are enabled for the instance.

entries.title: Vacuum, bloat and index health monitored
entries.requirement: Autovacuum is enabled and tuned for large or hot tables, and table bloat, dead tuples and unused or missing indexes are monitored, with pg_stat_statements enabled for query analysis.
entries.best_practice: Alert on autovacuum lag and transaction ID wraparound distance; review top queries regularly.

monitoring.signal: dead tuples, bloat estimate, wraparound age and pg_stat_statements

verification.criteria: Database health metrics are collected and reviewed.

entries.title: Migration lock safety
entries.requirement: Migrations avoid long exclusive locks: indexes are created concurrently, columns added with defaults safely, and a lock_timeout is set for migration sessions.
entries.best_practice: Break large changes into expand and contract steps; test migration duration on production-sized data.

monitoring.signal: blocked queries during migrations

verification.criteria: Migration scripts use safe patterns for large tables.

data_oracle.title: Oracle Database
data_oracle.description: Oracle Database requirements, extending the general relational database module.

entry_extensions.oracle_feature: the Oracle feature, parameter or driver property involved

entries.title: Pooling with Universal Connection Pool and fast failover
entries.requirement: The application uses Oracle UCP (or a pool with equivalent validation) with connection validation, sensible sizing against the database session limit, and FAN or Application Continuity so RAC or Data Guard failover is handled without errors reaching users.
entries.best_practice: Enable FAN through ONS; set connection validation on borrow; use service names, not instance names; size pools to the processes and sessions budget.

monitoring.signal: UCP pool statistics
sessions versus limit and failover events

verification.criteria: Pool settings are explicit and failover-aware.

entries.oracle_feature: UCP, Fast Application Notification (FAN), Application Continuity

entries.title: Encrypted connections with wallet-based credentials
entries.requirement: Connections use TLS (TCPS) or native network encryption with server verification, and credentials are stored in an Oracle wallet or secrets manager, not in connection strings.
entries.best_practice: Enforce encryption on the server side (SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_SERVER=REQUIRED); use external authentication for services.

monitoring.signal: sessions by encryption status

verification.criteria: TLS is on for the connection string and no credentials are embedded in it.

entries.oracle_feature: Native Network Encryption or TCPS, Oracle wallet

entries.title: Bind variables and statement timeouts
entries.requirement: SQL uses bind variables (avoiding hard parses and injection), the driver sets query timeouts, and Resource Manager limits runaway sessions.
entries.best_practice: Use consumer groups per application; set DEFAULT_CLASS limits; monitor hard parse ratio.

monitoring.signal: AWR and ASH top SQL, parse ratios

verification.criteria: Bind variables and timeouts are used.

entries.oracle_feature: bind variables, query timeout, Resource Manager

entries.title: Data Guard or RAC for availability, tested failover
entries.requirement: Production databases run with Data Guard (with defined protection mode) or RAC, backup with RMAN or a managed service, and failover and restore are tested.
entries.best_practice: Use Fast-Start Failover with an observer; test switchover; store backups in a separate failure domain.
entries.audit_requirement: Failover and restore tests recorded.

monitoring.signal: apply lag, transport lag and backup status

verification.criteria: Standby and backup arrangements are documented and tested.

entries.title: Unified auditing enabled for sensitive activity
entries.requirement: Unified auditing captures privileged actions, logins and access to sensitive tables, with retention, and tablespaces holding sensitive data use Transparent Data Encryption.
entries.best_practice: Ship audit records off the database; protect the audit trail; manage keys in a wallet or HSM.
entries.audit_requirement: Audit trail retained and reviewed per policy.

monitoring.signal: unified audit trail events

verification.criteria: Audit policies and TDE are enabled.

entries.oracle_feature: Unified Auditing policies, Transparent Data Encryption

data_sqlserver.title: Microsoft SQL Server
data_sqlserver.description: Microsoft SQL Server requirements, extending the general relational database module.

entry_extensions.sqlserver_feature: the SQL Server feature or connection string keyword involved

entries.title: Availability group listener and multi-subnet failover
entries.requirement: Applications connect to the availability group listener with MultiSubnetFailover enabled and connection retry, so failover completes without long connection stalls.
entries.best_practice: Set ConnectRetryCount and interval; use ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly for read scale-out; test planned and unplanned failover.

monitoring.signal: availability group synchronisation state and failover events

verification.criteria: Connection strings target the listener with failover keywords.

entries.title: Encrypted connections with certificate validation
entries.requirement: Connection strings require encryption and validate the server certificate (Encrypt true, TrustServerCertificate false), and the server enforces encryption.
entries.best_practice: Use current driver defaults (encrypt on by default in recent Microsoft drivers); manage the CA in the trust store.

monitoring.signal: sessions by encrypt_option in sys.dm_exec_connections

verification.criteria: Encrypt is true, certificates are validated and no credentials are in the connection string.

entries.title: Explicit command timeouts and pool limits
entries.requirement: Command timeout, connect timeout and maximum pool size are set explicitly (the client default command timeout is 30 seconds, and pool default is 100).
entries.best_practice: Set command timeout per operation type; size pools to the session budget; keep transactions short.

monitoring.signal: database call response time and failure rate
sessions and blocked processes

verification.criteria: Timeout and pool settings are explicit.

entries.sqlserver_feature: CommandTimeout, Max Pool Size, Connect Timeout

entries.title: Transparent Data Encryption and SQL Server Audit
entries.requirement: Databases with sensitive data use TDE with managed keys, and SQL Server Audit records logins, privileged actions and access to sensitive tables with retention.
entries.best_practice: Back up certificates and keys separately; write audits to a protected location or the platform log service.
entries.audit_requirement: Audit files retained per policy.

monitoring.signal: SQL Server Audit events

verification.criteria: TDE and audit specifications are enabled.

entries.title: Statistics, indexes and Query Store
entries.requirement: Query Store is enabled, index and statistics maintenance is scheduled, and plan regressions and blocking are monitored.
entries.best_practice: Use automatic tuning where appropriate; alert on long blocking chains and tempdb contention.

monitoring.signal: Query Store regressions, blocking and tempdb usage

verification.criteria: Query Store and maintenance jobs are active.

data_bigquery.title: BigQuery
data_bigquery.description: Requirements for services that read or write Google BigQuery (analytics stores and data pipelines).

entry_extensions.bigquery_feature: the BigQuery feature, quota or setting involved

entries.title: Query cost and quota guardrails
entries.requirement: Queries set maximum bytes billed, tables are partitioned and clustered with require-partition-filter where large, and project or user quotas and slot reservations are sized and monitored.
entries.best_practice: Use dry runs in CI; label jobs by service; set custom quotas per user or project; avoid SELECT * on wide tables.
entries.audit_requirement: Query costs are attributed to the owning service through labels.

monitoring.signal: bytes processed and slot usage from INFORMATION_SCHEMA jobs views

verification.criteria: Query jobs set maximum bytes billed and large tables are partitioned.

entries.title: Job timeouts, retries and idempotent job identifiers
entries.requirement: Query and load jobs set explicit timeouts, retry transient errors with backoff, and use deterministic job ids so a retried load or insert is not applied twice.
entries.best_practice: Poll long jobs asynchronously; use insertId or the Storage Write API with exactly-once semantics for streaming; handle quota errors with backoff.

monitoring.signal: job failure and retry counts by error reason
outbound call response time and failure rate to bigquery.googleapis.com

verification.criteria: BigQuery calls have timeouts, bounded retries and idempotency.

entries.title: Least-privilege IAM and customer-managed keys where required
entries.requirement: Datasets grant roles to service accounts at the narrowest scope (dataset or table, authorised views for shared data), and datasets with sensitive data use customer-managed encryption keys where policy requires.
entries.best_practice: Separate read and write identities; avoid project-wide Data Editor; use column-level security for sensitive columns.
entries.audit_requirement: Data Access audit logs enabled for BigQuery and retained.

monitoring.signal: Cloud Audit Logs data access events for BigQuery

verification.criteria: Dataset IAM bindings are narrow and CMEK is set where required.

entries.bigquery_feature: IAM, CMEK, authorised views, column-level security

entries.title: Table expiration, retention and recoverability
entries.requirement: Datasets and tables have explicit expiration and retention, time travel and fail-safe windows are understood, and critical tables have snapshots or exports for recovery.
entries.best_practice: Set default table expiration for scratch datasets; use table snapshots for critical data; document the recovery procedure.
entries.audit_requirement: Retention settings evidenced per dataset.

monitoring.signal: storage by dataset and snapshot age

verification.criteria: Retention and snapshot settings are declared.

entries.bigquery_feature: default_table_expiration_ms, time travel window, table snapshots

entries.title: Pipeline freshness and failure monitoring
entries.requirement: Data pipelines that load BigQuery have freshness and volume monitors (last successful load, row counts) with alerts, so silent staleness is detected.
entries.best_practice: Emit a freshness metric per table; alert when data is older than the agreed SLO; verify row counts and schema on load.

monitoring.signal: data freshness and load success per table

verification.criteria: Freshness SLOs and alerts exist per critical table.

data_gcp_managed.title: Managed cloud databases on Google Cloud
data_gcp_managed.description: Requirements for managed databases on Google Cloud (Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, Bigtable, Firestore, Memorystore) that GKE workloads connect to. GKE itself is the gke module.

entry_extensions.gcp_resource: the Google Cloud resource type or setting involved

entries.title: High availability configuration for the managed database
entries.requirement: Production Cloud SQL instances use regional (high availability) configuration, and AlloyDB or Spanner are deployed in a topology that meets the availability target, with maintenance windows chosen deliberately.
entries.best_practice: Test failover; use read replicas for read scale; set maintenance windows and deny-maintenance periods around peak business events.

monitoring.signal: Cloud Monitoring instance state, replication lag and failover events
database call failure rate during failover as seen by callers

verification.criteria: availability_type is REGIONAL (or equivalent HA setting) for production database resources.

entries.gcp_resource: google_sql_database_instance availability_type = REGIONAL, AlloyDB, Spanner regional or multi-region

entries.title: Private connectivity and authenticated connection through the connector or proxy
entries.requirement: Applications reach managed databases over private IP through the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy or a language connector (mutual TLS and IAM authorisation), preferably with IAM database authentication instead of static passwords, and public IP access is disabled or restricted.
entries.best_practice: Run the proxy as a sidecar or use the in-process connector; give each workload its own service account through Workload Identity; keep authorised networks empty.
entries.audit_requirement: Connection and IAM authentication events are captured in Cloud Audit Logs.

monitoring.signal: connections by source and authentication method

verification.criteria: ipv4_enabled is false or authorised networks are narrow, and the connector or proxy is used.

entries.gcp_resource: private IP, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy or language connectors, IAM database authentication

entries.title: Backups, point-in-time recovery, deletion protection and encryption
entries.requirement: Instances have automated backups with point-in-time recovery enabled, deletion protection set, and customer-managed encryption keys where policy requires.
entries.best_practice: Retain backups per policy; test restore into a new instance; protect keys with separate IAM.
entries.audit_requirement: Backup and key usage logs retained.

monitoring.signal: backup status and last successful backup age

verification.criteria: Backup, PITR and deletion protection attributes are set on database resources.

entries.title: Connection limits sized for proxies and replicas
entries.requirement: Connection pool sizes multiplied by replica counts, plus proxy overhead, stay within the instance connection limit, and managed connection pooling is used when many replicas connect.
entries.best_practice: Use built-in managed connection pooling where available; alert at 80 percent of max connections.

monitoring.signal: database connections versus limit
application pool saturation

verification.criteria: pool size times maximum replicas is below the instance connection limit.

entries.gcp_resource: max_connections database flag, connection pooling (managed pooler)

caching.title: Caching
caching.description: Requirements for in-process caches (Caffeine, Ehcache) and distributed caches (Redis, Memcached, Hazelcast). This module goes beyond the brief's named list because the pilot service uses Spring Cache with Caffeine.

entry_extensions.cache_kind: in_process | distributed: whether the requirement applies to in-process caches, distributed caches, or both

entries.title: Bounded size and explicit expiry
entries.requirement: Every cache has a maximum size (or memory limit) and a time-to-live or expiry policy, so it cannot grow without bound or serve indefinitely stale data.
entries.best_practice: Set maximumSize and expireAfterWrite (or Redis maxmemory with an eviction policy and key TTLs); choose TTLs from the staleness the business tolerates.

monitoring.signal: cache size, evictions and hit ratio
JVM or process memory growth

verification.criteria: Each cache pattern lists a size bound and expiry, or configuration exists for them.

entries.title: Cache failure never fails the request when the source is available
entries.requirement: If a distributed cache is unreachable or slow, the service falls back to the source of truth (with timeouts and a circuit breaker on the cache client) rather than failing requests.
entries.best_practice: Short client timeouts; treat cache errors as misses; protect the source from a thundering herd with rate limits.

monitoring.signal: response time and failure rate of calls to the cache service
cache client errors and timeouts

verification.criteria: A distributed cache dependency is classified gracefully_degradable, or has a documented reason for hard failure.

entries.title: Stampede protection and warm-up
entries.requirement: Concurrent misses for the same key are coalesced (loading cache, single flight), expiry is jittered, and cold-start warm-up is defined for caches that protect a slow source.
entries.best_practice: Use loading caches with refreshAfterWrite; add TTL jitter; avoid all pods expiring together.

monitoring.signal: load time and load failure counts
source dependency request rate after deployments

verification.criteria: Loading or single-flight semantics are used for hot keys.

entries.title: Sensitive data is not cached without protection
entries.requirement: Personal or secret data is not cached (or is cached only in encrypted, access-controlled stores with short TTLs), and per-user cache keys prevent cross-user leakage.
entries.best_practice: Classify cached data; include tenant and user in keys; require TLS and authentication for distributed caches.
entries.audit_requirement: Cached data classes are documented for privacy review.

monitoring.signal: cache access by service identity

verification.criteria: Cached methods do not return personal data unless justified.

entries.title: Distributed cache is secured and highly available
entries.requirement: Redis, Memcached or Hazelcast clusters require authentication and TLS, run with replication or managed HA, and have a defined behaviour on node loss.
entries.best_practice: Use managed offerings with HA tiers; restrict network access; set persistence deliberately.
entries.audit_requirement: Access and configuration changes are logged.

monitoring.signal: cache node health, memory use and replication status

verification.criteria: Distributed cache instances are replicated and require TLS and authentication.

gke.title: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
gke.description: Requirements for workloads on Google Kubernetes Engine, in addition to the Kubernetes module. Applies when GKE clusters (Terraform google_container_*) or Google-hosted container images are found.

entry_extensions.gcp_resource: the Google Cloud resource type or setting involved

entries.title: Regional cluster with managed node lifecycle
entries.requirement: Production clusters are regional, subscribe to a release channel, and node pools have auto-repair and auto-upgrade enabled with surge upgrade settings and maintenance windows chosen deliberately.
entries.best_practice: Spread nodes across at least three zones; use surge upgrades with maxSurge and maxUnavailable sized to keep capacity; avoid pinning cluster versions that fall out of support.
entries.audit_requirement: Cluster and node pool changes are captured in Cloud Audit Logs.

monitoring.signal: node pool health, upgrade status and autoscaler events

verification.criteria: Cluster resources are regional with a release channel and auto-repair and auto-upgrade set on node pools.

entries.gcp_resource: google_container_cluster (regional), release_channel, node_pool management auto_repair and auto_upgrade

entries.title: Workload Identity and private cluster networking
entries.requirement: Workloads reach Google Cloud APIs through Workload Identity (no node service account keys or exported keys), nodes are private, and the control plane endpoint is restricted with authorised networks.
entries.best_practice: Bind one Kubernetes service account to one Google service account with the minimum roles; disable legacy metadata endpoints; use VPC-native clusters.
entries.audit_requirement: IAM and Workload Identity bindings are reviewed on a schedule.

monitoring.signal: Cloud Audit Logs for IAM use by workload identities

verification.criteria: Workload Identity is configured and workloads use a dedicated service account with no static keys.

entries.title: Node pools sized and autoscaled for the workload classes
entries.requirement: Node pools are separated by workload class, use cluster or node auto-provisioning with explicit minimum and maximum sizes, and machine types fit the pods' requests so scheduling is not fragmented.
entries.best_practice: Set requests on every pod (Autopilot bills by requests); keep headroom for surge and node failure; use spot capacity only for tolerant workloads.

monitoring.signal: node utilisation, unschedulable pods and autoscaler decisions

verification.criteria: Node pool autoscaling bounds are set and pods declare requests.

entries.gcp_resource: node_pool autoscaling, machine_type, Autopilot or Standard mode

entries.title: Image provenance and vulnerability scanning
entries.requirement: Images come from Artifact Registry with vulnerability scanning enabled, are pinned by tag or digest, and clusters enforce Binary Authorization where policy requires signed images.
entries.best_practice: Scan on push and continuously; block deployment of critical vulnerabilities; keep base images current.
entries.audit_requirement: Scan results and attestations retained per release.

monitoring.signal: image vulnerabilities by severity and Binary Authorization denials

verification.criteria: Images are from a governed registry and carry explicit versions.

entries.title: Cluster logging, monitoring and audit enabled
entries.requirement: System and workload logging and monitoring are enabled for the cluster, control plane audit logs are retained, and dataplane network policy enforcement is on.
entries.best_practice: Enable Cloud Audit Logs for admin and data access where needed; use GKE Dataplane V2 or Calico for network policy enforcement.
entries.audit_requirement: Audit and admin activity logs retained per policy.

monitoring.signal: log ingestion and control plane audit log volume

verification.criteria: Logging, monitoring and network policy enforcement are configured on the cluster.

entries.gcp_resource: logging_config, monitoring_config, managed Prometheus, Kubernetes audit logs

observability_dynatrace.title: Dynatrace observability
observability_dynatrace.description: Requirements for how a service is onboarded and operated in Dynatrace. Applies when Dynatrace is the active observability provider.

entry_extensions.dynatrace_feature: the Dynatrace capability the requirement is expressed through

entries.title: OneAgent full-stack monitoring on every process
entries.requirement: OneAgent is deployed on all hosts or injected into all pods of the service (through the Dynatrace Operator on Kubernetes), at a supported version, with deep monitoring enabled for the service's technology.
entries.best_practice: Use the Operator's cloud-native full-stack mode; keep agents on the automatic update schedule; restrict injection by namespace labels deliberately.
entries.audit_requirement: Agent versions and coverage are reported periodically.

monitoring.signal: OneAgent connectivity, version and monitored process count

verification.criteria: The bound service id resolves to a monitored service whose processes report through OneAgent.

entries.title: Service ownership, tags and naming
entries.requirement: Every service carries ownership, environment and tier tags, sits in the right management zone or segment, and has meaningful service and request names, so problems route to the correct team.
entries.best_practice: Derive tags from Kubernetes labels and annotations; define naming rules; keep ownership in a single source.
entries.audit_requirement: Ownership records are reviewed periodically.

monitoring.signal: services without owner or environment tags

verification.criteria: The service has owner, environment and tier tags.

entries.dynatrace_feature: automatic tags, management zones, ownership, request naming

entries.title: Key requests, SLOs and alerting profiles for critical operations
entries.requirement: The critical business operations are marked as key requests, have SLOs with burn-rate alerting, and anomaly detection is tuned (fixed thresholds where baselining is unsuitable), with alerts routed to the owning team.
entries.best_practice: Derive key requests from the business context and transaction flows; use multi-window burn-rate alerts; link problems to runbooks.
entries.audit_requirement: SLO and alert configuration changes are versioned.

monitoring.signal: key request response time and failure rate
SLO status and burn rate

verification.criteria: Each key business operation maps to a key request with an SLO and alert.

entries.dynatrace_feature: key requests, SLOs, anomaly detection, alerting profiles

entries.title: Deployment events and version tagging
entries.requirement: The CI/CD pipeline posts deployment events to Dynatrace and services report their version, so releases correlate with changes in error rate or latency.
entries.best_practice: Send events from the pipeline with commit, build and environment; use them as inputs to release validation.

monitoring.signal: deployment events per service

verification.criteria: A pipeline step sends a deployment event.

entries.title: Log ingestion correlated with traces
entries.requirement: Application logs are ingested with retention set deliberately, and log records carry trace context so they appear on the distributed trace.
entries.best_practice: Ingest structured JSON logs; set log storage retention per bucket; mask sensitive fields before ingest.
entries.audit_requirement: Log retention settings evidenced.

monitoring.signal: ingested log volume and retention bucket usage

verification.criteria: Logs from the service are present on its traces and retention is configured.

entries.title: Custom instrumentation only for the gaps, ingested with correct dimensions
entries.requirement: Metrics from the application-level instrumentation catalogue and business metrics are ingested only where OneAgent has no equivalent, with bounded dimensions and consistent naming, and every custom metric has an owner.
entries.best_practice: Check the OneAgent default catalogue first; review custom metric cardinality and cost; document the purpose of each custom metric.

monitoring.signal: ingested custom metric count and dimension cardinality

verification.criteria: Custom metrics do not duplicate default signals and have bounded dimensions.

entries.dynatrace_feature: metric ingestion (Micrometer, OTLP), OpenTelemetry, custom metrics

capacity_scaling.title: Capacity and scaling
capacity_scaling.description: Capacity posture across the infrastructure layer (requests and limits, autoscaling, replicas, disruption budgets) and the application layer (connection pools, thread pools, rate limiters). Evaluated against the Stage 1 infrastructure analysis and the application capacity settings from code analysis.

entry_extensions.layer: infrastructure | application | cross_layer: which layer's Stage 1 data is evaluated
entry_extensions.explicit_setting_required: true when the requirement is that a value is set explicitly rather than left at a framework default

entries.title: Resource requests and limits defined for every container
entries.requirement: Every container declares CPU and memory requests and a memory limit (and a CPU limit or a documented decision not to set one).
entries.best_practice: Requests reflect steady-state usage (they drive scheduling and autoscaling); memory limit above the working set with headroom; memory request equal to the limit for predictable eviction behaviour; a CPU limit only where throttling is understood.
entries.audit_requirement: Resource sizing decisions are recorded with the load test or production usage that justified them.

monitoring.signal: container CPU and memory usage against requests and limits
process CPU usage and working-set memory

verification.criteria: Every container of every workload has non-empty requests and limits for cpu and memory; containers with neither are a finding.

entries.title: Autoscaling configured with sensible thresholds
entries.requirement: Variable-load workloads have horizontal autoscaling with a minimum of at least two replicas, a maximum that bounds cost and downstream load, and a utilisation target with headroom.
entries.best_practice: Scale on a metric that tracks load (CPU, requests per second, queue depth) at a target that leaves headroom (commonly 50 to 70 percent CPU); set scale-down stabilisation to avoid flapping; make sure requests are set, because utilisation targets are relative to requests.
entries.audit_requirement: Autoscaling limits and targets are reviewed alongside capacity tests.

monitoring.signal: desired versus current replicas and scaling events
request rate and response time during scale events

verification.criteria: An autoscaler targets each variable-load workload, min_replicas is at least 2, max_replicas is bounded, and a metric with a target value is defined. Where replica-count telemetry is available, a policy never observed triggering (replica count constant throughout the window) is a finding distinct from the config being present at all.

entries.title: Replica count gives redundancy, not a single point of failure
entries.requirement: Every production workload runs at least two replicas spread across failure domains.
entries.best_practice: Use pod anti-affinity or topology spread constraints across nodes and zones; never rely on a single replica for a user-facing service; size N+1 for node loss.
entries.audit_requirement: Redundancy level is stated in the service's availability target.

monitoring.signal: ready replicas versus desired, per zone
process availability per instance

verification.criteria: Each workload has replicas (or autoscaler min_replicas) of at least 2; a single replica, or replicas with no anti-affinity or topology spread, is a finding.

entries.title: Pod disruption budget protects multi-replica workloads
entries.requirement: Workloads with more than one replica have a PodDisruptionBudget that keeps a minimum number available during voluntary disruptions (node drains, upgrades).
entries.best_practice: Set minAvailable or maxUnavailable so a drain cannot remove all replicas; do not set a budget that blocks all disruptions permanently.

monitoring.signal: allowed disruptions on the budget

verification.criteria: Every workload with two or more replicas is selected by a PodDisruptionBudget.

entries.title: Database connection pool size set explicitly
entries.requirement: The maximum connection pool size, minimum idle, connection timeout and max lifetime are set explicitly in application configuration rather than left at framework defaults.
entries.best_practice: Size the pool from the database's connection budget divided by the replica count at maximum scale, not from thread counts; set an acquisition timeout that fails fast; keep max lifetime below the database or proxy idle timeout.

monitoring.signal: pool active, idle, pending and timeout counters
database call response time and failure rate from the calling service

verification.criteria: For each datastore dependency there is a db_pool capacity setting with origin explicit; origin framework_default is a finding.

entries.title: Thread pools and executors configured explicitly
entries.requirement: Server request threads, async executors and scheduler pools have explicit sizes and bounded queues.
entries.best_practice: Bound queues and choose a rejection policy; isolate blocking work on its own pool; keep total threads consistent with the container CPU limit.

monitoring.signal: executor active, queued and rejected counts
JVM or runtime thread count

verification.criteria: thread_pool and server_connections capacity settings exist with origin explicit; only framework defaults is a finding.

entries.title: Rate limits and backpressure thresholds set for inbound and outbound traffic
entries.requirement: Entry points exposed to untrusted or bursty callers have a rate limit (in the application, gateway or mesh), and calls to constrained dependencies are limited by a rate limiter or bulkhead.
entries.best_practice: Limit per client and per route; return 429 with Retry-After; shed load before saturation; protect downstream dependencies with concurrency limits.

monitoring.signal: permitted versus rejected calls
HTTP 429 and 503 response rate

verification.criteria: A rate_limiter capacity setting or rate_limiter/bulkhead pattern exists for public entry points, or a gateway or mesh limit is configured.

entries.title: Application limits consistent with infrastructure limits
entries.requirement: Application pool and thread settings fit inside the container limits and the aggregate load they can place on shared dependencies at maximum replicas.
entries.best_practice: Check pool size times maximum replicas against the database connection limit; keep JVM heap below the container memory limit with headroom for non-heap memory; keep worker threads consistent with the CPU request.
entries.audit_requirement: Capacity model (per-replica limits and dependency budgets) is kept with the service documentation.

monitoring.signal: pool utilisation across replicas
container memory working set against the limit

verification.criteria: db_pool size multiplied by the maximum replica count does not exceed the datastore's connection limit, and configured heap or memory settings are below the container memory limit.

entries.title: Termination grace period covers connection draining
entries.requirement: terminationGracePeriodSeconds is set explicitly and is longer than the application's drain time.
entries.best_practice: Pair with a preStop delay and application graceful shutdown; avoid the 30 second default when in-flight work can run longer.

monitoring.signal: pods killed with SIGKILL after grace period expiry

verification.criteria: termination_grace_period_seconds is present for each workload.

entries.title: Rollout capacity headroom
entries.requirement: Rolling update parameters (maxSurge, maxUnavailable) keep enough capacity serving during a rollout.
entries.best_practice: Use maxUnavailable 0 (or a small fraction) with maxSurge above 0 for user-facing services so capacity never drops during a deploy.

monitoring.signal: available replicas during rollout

verification.criteria: Rolling strategy workloads set max_unavailable low enough that capacity is preserved; Recreate on a user-facing workload is a finding.

deployment_rollback_safety.title: Deployment and rollback safety
deployment_rollback_safety.description: Whether releases reach production through a controlled strategy, can be reverted quickly, and keep database changes separate and reviewable. Evaluated against the CI/CD pipeline data (strategy, rollback, migrations) from Stage 1 infrastructure analysis.

entry_extensions.pipeline_system: the CI/CD systems the requirement applies to when it is system specific

entries.title: Defined deployment strategy rather than an all-at-once rollout
entries.requirement: Production deployments use a defined strategy (rolling with surge limits, blue-green or canary), not an in-place recreate of all instances at once.
entries.best_practice: Prefer canary or blue-green for user-facing services with automated verification between steps; a rolling update is acceptable when readiness gates and surge limits are set.
entries.audit_requirement: The strategy used for each production release is recorded in the deployment log.

monitoring.signal: deployment events and rollout progress
error rate and response time around deployment events

verification.criteria: Each deploying pipeline has deployment_strategy of rolling, blue_green or canary; recreate, unknown or none is a finding.

entries.title: Automated or documented rollback path
entries.requirement: Every deploying pipeline has an automated rollback trigger (health or metric based) or a documented, tested manual rollback step.
entries.best_practice: Automate rollback on failed health checks or SLO burn during the rollout; keep the previous version's artifacts and configuration available; rehearse the manual path.
entries.audit_requirement: Every rollback is recorded with its trigger and approver.

monitoring.signal: rollback events per service
failure rate on the new version during rollout

verification.criteria: rollback.mode is automated or manual for every deploying pipeline; none_defined is a finding.

entries.title: Database migrations run as a separate, reviewable step
entries.requirement: Schema migrations run as their own pipeline stage or job that can be reviewed, approved and re-run independently of the application rollout, not bundled invisibly into application start-up.
entries.best_practice: Run migrations from a dedicated job before the application step; require review of the migration scripts; avoid application-start-up auto migration on multi-replica production deployments.
entries.audit_requirement: Migration scripts, approvals and execution results are retained for audit.

monitoring.signal: migration job status and duration
migration tool execution log

verification.criteria: If a migration tool is present in the application or pipeline, the pipeline runs it as a separate step (separate_step true); embedded application start-up migration with no pipeline step is a finding.

entries.title: Backward-compatible (expand and contract) migrations
entries.requirement: Each migration is compatible with both the previous and the new application version so a rollback of the application does not need a database rollback.
entries.best_practice: Use expand-then-contract; add columns as nullable or defaulted; never drop or rename in the same release that stops using it; test the old version against the new schema.
entries.audit_requirement: Destructive migrations require explicit approval.

monitoring.signal: errors from the previous version after a schema change

verification.criteria: Migration scripts reviewed for backward compatibility; a migration tool with versioned scripts is in use.

entries.title: Health-gated rollout
entries.requirement: New instances receive traffic only after passing readiness, and a rollout stops if new instances do not become ready in a bounded time.
entries.best_practice: Define readiness and startup probes; set progress deadlines and minimum ready seconds; keep maxUnavailable at 0 for user-facing services.

monitoring.signal: rollout progress and failed-ready instances

verification.criteria: Every deployed container has a readiness probe.

entries.title: Quality and approval gates before production
entries.requirement: The pipeline runs automated tests and security checks before the deploy step and requires approval for production according to policy.
entries.best_practice: Build once and promote the same artifact; run unit, integration and vulnerability scans as required stages; require approval only where policy demands it, and record it.
entries.audit_requirement: Approvals, test results and scan results are retained per release.

monitoring.signal: pipeline stage results and lead time

verification.criteria: The pipeline definition contains test and scan stages ahead of the deploy step and an approval step for production where policy requires.

entries.title: Immutable, versioned artifacts
entries.requirement: Deployed container images are referenced by an immutable version or digest, never a mutable tag such as latest.
entries.best_practice: Tag by commit or build number; pin digests in production manifests; promote the same image across environments.
entries.audit_requirement: The running image can be traced to a commit and build.

monitoring.signal: running image version per workload

verification.criteria: No workload image uses the latest tag or omits a tag.

entries.title: Post-deployment verification tied to monitoring
entries.requirement: A release is verified against live telemetry (error rate, latency) for a bounded window, and a regression triggers rollback or halts progression.
entries.best_practice: Use the observability platform's deployment events and automated release validation as a pipeline gate.
entries.audit_requirement: Verification results are stored with the release record.

monitoring.signal: service failure rate and response time compared with the pre-release baseline
deployment event markers

verification.criteria: The pipeline has an automated verification or automated rollback step after deployment.

dependency_criticality.title: Dependency criticality
dependency_criticality.description: Whether each dependency whose outage fails a request has either a justified reason for having no degradation handling or a circuit breaker, fallback, cache or similar pattern, worked through in blast-radius order. Evaluated against the dependency classification and blast radius produced during Stage 1 transaction flow tracing.

entry_extensions.prioritisation: how Stage 3 should order findings for this entry (for example descending blast radius)

entries.title: Every hard failure dependency is justified or protected
entries.requirement: Each dependency classified as hard_failure has either a recorded justification for lacking degradation handling (for example the data is the system of record and a stale answer would be wrong) or a circuit breaker, fallback, cache or comparable pattern applied.
entries.best_practice: For read paths prefer a cache or stale-serving fallback; for optional enrichments return a reduced response; for the system of record accept the hard dependency but make it highly available and fast to fail; document the decision either way.
entries.audit_requirement: Each accepted hard dependency and its justification is recorded and re-reviewed on architecture change.

monitoring.signal: availability, failure rate and response time of the dependency's service
breaker state and fallback invocation counters where a pattern exists

verification.criteria: For every classification hard_failure, protecting_patterns is non-empty or the rationale gives a justification; otherwise it is a finding to recommend a circuit breaker, fallback or cache. A dependency the observability provider shows in the live topology but that was never classified at all (because code/infra analysis never found it) is the same finding by extension: it has no recorded protection either, and is a distinct, runtime-only instance of this gap.

entries.prioritisation: descending blast radius (number of flows and entry points that fail)

entries.title: Findings are prioritised by blast radius
entries.requirement: Remediation of dependency findings is ordered by blast radius, largest first, so the dependencies that would fail the most transactions are addressed first.
entries.best_practice: Weight by the business importance of the failed flows (from the business context) as well as their number.

monitoring.signal: request volume of the entry points in each blast radius

verification.criteria: Dependencies are ranked by the size of blast_radius and the business importance of the affected entry points.

entries.title: Hard failure dependencies fail fast
entries.requirement: A hard failure dependency has a timeout (and where retries apply, a bounded retry), so its outage becomes a fast error instead of exhausting threads and connections.
entries.best_practice: Timeouts shorter than the caller's; bulkhead or pool isolation per dependency; clear error mapping to the caller.

monitoring.signal: response time percentiles of calls to the dependency
pool acquisition timeouts and pending requests

verification.criteria: Each hard_failure dependency has a timeout pattern or a configured client or pool timeout.

entries.title: Degraded behaviour of degradable dependencies is defined and exercised
entries.requirement: For each gracefully_degradable dependency the reduced behaviour (stale data, default response, feature disabled) is specified, and it is exercised in tests or fault-injection drills.
entries.best_practice: Test with the dependency down and slow; surface degraded mode in a response header or metric so it is visible.
entries.audit_requirement: Fault-injection or game-day results are retained.

monitoring.signal: fallback or degraded-mode invocation counter
cache hit ratio and stale-serve counters

verification.criteria: Each degradable dependency names its protecting pattern and the flows that degrade; a test or drill exists (manual review).

entries.title: Mesh-layer protection is recognised
entries.requirement: A dependency with no resilience pattern in application code is considered protected only if a mesh-level retry, timeout or circuit-breaking policy applies to its host.
entries.best_practice: Keep resilience in one layer per concern; document which layer owns retries and timeouts; verify mesh policy host names match the real dependency host.

monitoring.signal: mesh proxy retry, timeout and outlier-detection counters

verification.criteria: For hard_failure dependencies without code-level patterns, a dependency_mesh_policies cross reference shows a matching mesh policy.

entries.title: Shared data stores and caches are not single points of failure
entries.requirement: Every datastore or cache classified as a dependency has a redundancy or recovery design (replicas, failover, backup and restore) appropriate to its blast radius.
entries.best_practice: Use managed high-availability tiers or replicated topologies; test failover; define RPO and RTO per datastore.
entries.audit_requirement: Backup, restore tests and RPO/RTO are documented and evidenced.

monitoring.signal: replication lag, failover events and backup success
availability of the database service as seen by callers

verification.criteria: Datastores in the dependency list run with replication or a managed HA tier, or the single-instance choice is justified (for example local development only).

entries.title: Dependency health is observable from the calling service
entries.requirement: The availability, latency and error rate of each dependency are visible from the caller's telemetry, with alerts for the hard failure dependencies.
entries.best_practice: Use the observability platform's automatic dependency detection; alert on dependency failure rate, not only on the caller's own errors.

monitoring.signal: service-to-service and service-to-database call metrics
metrics for dependencies that are not automatically detected

verification.criteria: Each classified dependency appears in the provider's topology with request metrics.

secrets_configuration.title: Secrets and configuration management
secrets_configuration.description: Whether credentials and sensitive values stay out of code and committed configuration and are sourced from an approved secrets manager, vault or Kubernetes secrets. Evaluated against the secrets handling data captured in Stage 1 code and infrastructure analysis.

entry_extensions.policy_dependent: true when the outcome depends on the organisation's secrets policy (for example plain env vars allowed or not)

entries.title: No hardcoded credentials or sensitive values in code or committed configuration
entries.requirement: Source files and committed configuration contain no passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys or credentials embedded in connection strings.
entries.best_practice: Reference secrets by name from the environment or a secrets manager; keep only placeholders (with no default secret value) in committed configuration; add secret scanning to pre-commit and CI; rotate anything that was ever committed.
entries.audit_requirement: Secret scanning results and remediation of exposed secrets are retained.

monitoring.signal: secret scanning alerts in the source control platform and CI

verification.criteria: No finding of kind hardcoded_credential, private_key, credentials_in_connection_string or plaintext_secret_manifest; default_value_in_placeholder findings are reviewed (a default that is a real credential is a finding, a demo default is noted).

entries.title: Secrets sourced from an approved secrets manager, vault or Kubernetes secrets
entries.requirement: Runtime secrets come from an approved store (a secrets manager or vault, or Kubernetes secrets populated from one) and are injected at deploy or run time.
entries.best_practice: Prefer a secrets manager with an operator or CSI driver (external secrets) over long-lived secrets baked into manifests; scope each secret to the workload that needs it.
entries.audit_requirement: Secret access is logged by the secrets platform and reviewed periodically.

monitoring.signal: secrets manager access logs and denied requests

verification.criteria: Each secret referenced by the application has a sourced_from mechanism of vault, secrets_manager, external_secrets or kubernetes_secret.

entries.title: Plain environment variables only where policy allows
entries.requirement: Where policy requires stronger handling than plain environment variables, secrets are delivered through a secrets manager, mounted files or an external-secrets mechanism rather than inline env values.
entries.best_practice: Environment variables sourced from Kubernetes secrets (secretKeyRef) are preferable to literal values; avoid printing the environment in logs or crash dumps; consider file mounts to avoid leaking through process listings.
entries.audit_requirement: The exception list of secrets allowed as plain env vars is approved and reviewed.

monitoring.signal: environment or configuration dumps in logs

verification.criteria: Secrets whose only source is environment_variable are checked against the policy on stronger handling; secret_env_var_supply cross references show each variable supplied by a secret reference.

entries.title: Kubernetes Secret manifests are not committed with values
entries.requirement: Secret manifests in the repository contain no real values (encrypted with sealed secrets, generated by an operator, or placeholders).
entries.best_practice: Use sealed or external secrets; base64 is encoding, not protection; restrict RBAC on Secret objects; enable encryption of secrets at rest in etcd.
entries.audit_requirement: Kubernetes API audit logs capture secret reads.

monitoring.signal: Kubernetes audit log entries for secret get and list

verification.criteria: No plaintext_secret_manifest finding; kubernetes_secret_definition cross references show inline_values_committed false.

entries.title: Credential rotation without redeploy
entries.requirement: Credentials can be rotated on a schedule and after a suspected leak without a code change, and the application picks up rotated values (reload, short-lived dynamic credentials, or a controlled restart).
entries.best_practice: Use dynamic short-lived database credentials or workload identity where available; rotate on a defined interval; test rotation.
entries.audit_requirement: Rotation dates are recorded and overdue rotations are reported.

monitoring.signal: credential age and rotation events
authentication failures after rotation

verification.criteria: A vault or secrets manager integration (or workload identity) is present so rotation does not need a code change.

entries.title: Environment-specific configuration is externalised
entries.requirement: Environment-specific and sensitive configuration is supplied through ConfigMaps, secrets or a configuration service, not baked into images or committed per-environment files with real values.
entries.best_practice: One artifact for all environments; configuration by injection; validate configuration at start-up.
entries.audit_requirement: Configuration changes are versioned and attributable.

monitoring.signal: configuration change events

verification.criteria: Configuration reaches containers through ConfigMap or secret references rather than literal values in the image.

entries.title: Least-privilege workload identity
entries.requirement: Workloads run under a dedicated service account with minimal permissions, as a non-root user, and reach cloud APIs through workload identity rather than static keys.
entries.best_practice: One service account per workload; drop capabilities; read-only root filesystem; no static cloud keys in secrets.
entries.audit_requirement: Service account bindings are reviewed on a schedule.

monitoring.signal: cloud audit logs for the workload identity

verification.criteria: Workloads set a service account other than default and run as non-root.

encryption_audit.title: Encryption and audit
encryption_audit.description: Encryption at rest, encryption in transit, and audit logging with retention. Evaluated against the encryption and audit evidence from Stage 1 code and infrastructure analysis (including mTLS enforced by a service mesh).

entry_extensions.domain: at_rest | in_transit | audit | retention: matches the domain field of the Stage 1 encryption and audit facts

entries.title: Databases and storage volumes are encrypted at rest
entries.requirement: Managed databases, persistent volumes, object storage and backups have encryption at rest enabled.
entries.best_practice: Use platform-managed encryption at minimum and customer-managed keys where policy requires; encrypt snapshots and backups with the same rigour.
entries.audit_requirement: Encryption configuration is evidenced for each data store holding sensitive data.

monitoring.signal: cloud configuration compliance checks for unencrypted disks, buckets and databases

verification.criteria: For every datastore and volume there is an at_rest fact with status enabled; disabled or missing is a finding (managed database attributes in Terraform count as evidence).

entries.title: Service-to-service and external calls use TLS
entries.requirement: Traffic between services and to external systems is encrypted with TLS, by the application or by mesh-enforced mTLS.
entries.best_practice: Enforce mTLS with the mesh in strict mode where a mesh exists; otherwise configure TLS in clients and servers; use modern protocol versions and verify certificates.
entries.audit_requirement: TLS policy and certificate issuance are documented; certificate expiry is monitored.

monitoring.signal: percentage of mesh traffic that is mTLS
certificate expiry countdown

verification.criteria: No in_transit fact with status plaintext or disabled for service-to-service or external calls, unless mesh mtls in strict mode covers the traffic (transport_encryption_mesh_and_code cross reference). Where the observability provider records a remote endpoint scheme for a live call, that runtime observation is evidence too: a call the code/config claims is TLS but is observed with a plaintext scheme is a finding, distinct from one caught by dataset facts alone.

entries.title: No plain HTTP endpoints that should be HTTPS
entries.requirement: Externally reachable endpoints terminate TLS, redirect HTTP to HTTPS and use HSTS; no internal URL in configuration uses http:// for a non-local dependency.
entries.best_practice: Terminate TLS at a managed ingress or gateway with automatic certificates; keep http:// only for loopback and health probes.

monitoring.signal: request count by protocol on the entry service
ingress TLS certificate validity

verification.criteria: Every ingress host is in tls_hosts; no plaintext in_transit fact for a non-local target.

entries.title: Database and cache connections use TLS
entries.requirement: Connections from the application to databases, caches and brokers require TLS with certificate verification.
entries.best_practice: Set the driver's TLS mode to verify the server certificate (for example verify-full); use private connectivity as an additional, not a substitute, control.

monitoring.signal: database sessions by encryption status

verification.criteria: Datastore connection strings and settings enable TLS; jdbc urls with ssl disabled or absent are a finding. A live connection the observability provider shows negotiated without TLS is a finding too, even if config claims otherwise.

entries.title: Authentication events are audit logged
entries.requirement: Logins, failed logins, token issuance, logouts and privilege elevation are recorded in an audit log with actor, time, source and outcome.
entries.best_practice: Emit audit events as a dedicated stream separate from application logs; include a trace id; do not record credentials.
entries.audit_requirement: Authentication audit records are retained per policy and protected from alteration.

monitoring.signal: authentication success and failure events per actor and source
failed authentication rate

verification.criteria: An audit fact or audit library covers authentication events.

entries.title: Sensitive data access is audit logged
entries.requirement: Reads and writes of sensitive or regulated data are recorded with who, what, when and from where.
entries.best_practice: Log at the data access layer (repository or database audit) rather than relying on callers; record identifiers, not the data itself.
entries.audit_requirement: Data access audit logs are queryable for the retention period.

monitoring.signal: data access audit events for sensitive entities

verification.criteria: Audit coverage exists for each sensitive domain entity in the business context.

entries.title: Administrative actions are audit logged
entries.requirement: Administrative and configuration changes (user management, role changes, feature flags, infrastructure changes) are recorded in an audit trail.
entries.best_practice: Use platform audit logs for infrastructure and an application audit event for admin endpoints; alert on privileged actions outside change windows.
entries.audit_requirement: Administrative audit trail is retained and reviewed.

monitoring.signal: cloud and Kubernetes audit log events for privileged actions
application admin action events

verification.criteria: Admin entry points (routes such as /admin) and infrastructure changes are covered by audit logging.

entries.title: Audit and log retention is configured
entries.requirement: Audit logs have an explicit retention period that meets the regulatory and organisational requirement, and old records are archived or deleted on a defined schedule.
entries.best_practice: Set retention in the log platform and storage lifecycle rules; keep audit logs immutable (write-once) and off the host that produced them.
entries.audit_requirement: Retention settings are evidenced for each audit stream.

monitoring.signal: retention policy configuration and storage lifecycle status

verification.criteria: At least one retention fact with a value is found for the audit streams.

entries.title: Key management for encryption
entries.requirement: Encryption keys are managed in a KMS or HSM with rotation, separation of duties and access logging, not stored beside the data.
entries.best_practice: Use customer-managed keys where policy requires; automate rotation; restrict decrypt permissions to the workload identity.
entries.audit_requirement: Key usage and rotation logs are retained.

monitoring.signal: KMS key usage and rotation status

verification.criteria: Encrypted resources reference a KMS key (or a platform-managed key policy is documented).

entries.title: Modern TLS versions and ciphers
entries.requirement: TLS 1.2 or later only, with current cipher suites; legacy protocols and weak ciphers are disabled.
